An SPI rasterizer GPU,
from FPGA to a SKY130 chip

VGA controller · framebuffer · Bresenham lines · filled rectangles · outline and filled circles — driven by an Arduino over SPI. First on your PYNQ-Z2 with your video adapter, then the same gpu_core.v hardened with LibreLane and wrapped in a hand-built padframe with OpenROAD, exactly like your counter8_fullchip.

01

What we are building

read

The idea

One GPU design, one RTL file set, three builds. Only the parameters of gpu_core change, so the thing you debug on the FPGA is the thing that goes into silicon.

Build 1 · FPGA (PYNQ-Z2)Build 2 · ASIC v1Build 3 · ASIC v2 (Part 7)
Framebuffer320 × 240, double buffered40 × 30, single80 × 60, single
Pixel format8 bit RGB332 (256 colours)3 bit RGB111 (8 colours)8 bit RGB332
StorageBlock RAM (38 × RAMB36)3,600 standard-cell flip-flops5 × OpenRAM SRAM macros
Screen scaling2 × 216 × 168 × 8
Pixel clock25.000 MHz (MMCM)25.175 MHz oscillator25.175 MHz oscillator
CommandsCLEAR · LINE · RECT · CIRCLE (outline / filled) · SWAPsamesame
Signal pins4 SPI + 14 VGA + 4 LED11 GPIO + power-good16 GPIO + power-good
Verified hereRTL sim, Yosys xc7 estimateRTL + gate-level sim, synthesisRTL sim with the real OpenRAM model

Why the ASIC framebuffer is so small

Without an SRAM macro every pixel bit is a flip-flop plus its share of a large read multiplexer. 1,200 pixels × 3 bits already costs 83 % of the 0.17 mm² of cells; all the drawing engines together are about 17 %:

02

The pin protocol: SPI + READY

read

Why SPI + one READY pin

A rasterizer GPU receives commands, not pixels. Any cheap MCU (Arduino, ESP32, Pico) should drive it with its hardware SPI, and the ASIC padframe should stay small. So the host gets three outputs and one input:

  • SPI mode 0, write-only: CS, SCK, MOSI. No MISO needed.
  • gpu_ready: high when the GPU accepts the next command. This is the whole flow-control scheme: wait READY → send → repeat.
  • One command = one 10-byte frame while CS is low. It runs only when CS rises after exactly 80 bits. Short or long frames are ignored.

Command set

OpcodeNameABCDWhat the GPU doesGPU busy time
0x01CLEAR––––fills the whole (back) buffer with the colourW·H clocks · 3.07 ms FPGA, 48 µs ASIC
0x02LINEx0y0x1y1Bresenham, both end points drawn, off-screen pixels skippedmax(|dx|,|dy|) + 1 clocks
0x03RECTxywhfilled rectangle, clipped (negative x/y allowed)visible w·h clocks
0x04SWAP––––FPGA: flip buffers at the next vblank · ASIC: wait for vblank≤ 16.7 ms
0x05CIRCLEcxcyrfillmidpoint circle; D bit 0: 0 = outline, 1 = filled disc; clippedoutline ≈ 5.7·r · filled ≈ π·r² clocks

Colours

The colour byte is always RGB332. The FPGA repeats the MSBs to drive your 4-bit-per-channel adapter; the ASIC keeps only the top bit of each channel, so the same sketch works on both:

Name in sketchRGB332bits RRRGGGBBFPGA (RGB444 out)ASIC v1 (RGB111 out)
WHITE0xFF11111111FFF111
YELLOW0xFC11111100FF0110
CYAN0x1F000111110FF011
GREEN0x1C000111000F0010
MAGENTA0xE311100011F0F101
RED0xE011100000F00100
BLUE0x030000001100F001
ORANGE0xF011110000F90110
GREY0x921001001099A111
BLACK0x0000000000000000
!
Host timing rules
  • SCK ≤ core clock / 8 → ≤ 3 MHz at 25 MHz (the sketch uses 2 MHz).
  • Poll READY high before CS goes low; after CS goes high wait ≥ 1 µs before polling again (the GPU needs ~4 clocks to see CS).
  • Coordinates use the low 12 bits as signed values: −2048 … 2047; w/h the low 12 bits unsigned; r the low 11 bits (0 … 2047). Send them as int16, big endian.

One source of truth

rtl/ is the master copy. asic/src/ and asic_sram/src/ hold copies because LibreLane likes all sources inside its design folder. After editing rtl/, re-copy with cp rtl/*.v asic/src/.

01

The RTL, one module at a time

Seven small files. The three drawing engines only walk their shape and say "plot (x, y)"; clipping, colour and addressing are written once in gpu_core. For every module: the idea, the algorithm step by step, the ports, the code, and a waveform from the real simulation.

06

How the RTL is organised (read this first)

readverified

One interface for every drawing engine

Every engine — line, rectangle, circle — has the same shape:

PortMeaning
start + argumentsone-clock pulse from gpu_core; the arguments are valid in that clock and are copied inside
busyhigh from the clock after start until the last pixel; READY is low while any engine is busy
plot, x, y"(x, y) is a pixel of my shape" — one pixel per clock

The engines do not know the colour, the screen size (except for skipping invisible circle spans), the memory layout or which buffer is drawn. gpu_core picks the engine that is plotting, throws away off-screen pixels, computes y · W + x once and writes the latched colour. That is why each engine is short enough to read in one go, and why adding the circle needed no change to the framebuffer path.

Coding rules used in every file

RuleWhy
One clock (25 MHz) for everything; SPI pins and rst_n are synchronizedno clock-domain crossings inside, easy timing on FPGA and ASIC
Only control flops are reset (busy, counters, flags); datapath registers (coordinates, error terms, the command word) are loaded on starta reset needs a gate in front of every flop; on SKY130 that is area for nothing. Before start they show x in the waveforms — harmless, because plot is 0
Sign extension written out: {2{a[11]}, a}Verilator -Wall wants explicit widths, and it documents where numbers grow
Constants sized from parameters: FB_W[ADDR_BITS-1:0]no 32-bit integer creeping into comparisons
Lint-clean in all three builds (FPGA, ASIC v1, ASIC v2)LibreLane stops on lint errors; the FPGA build hides different warnings than the ASIC
!
A bug I hit while cleaning up — worth remembering

A concatenation {…} is always unsigned in Verilog, even if every part of it comes from a signed wire. My first version of the line engine compared e2 >= {dy[13], dy}; that silently became an unsigned compare (−3 looks like 32765), the line never reached its end point and READY stayed low. The fix is to put the extended value in its own wire signed first. Lint did not warn — the self-checking testbench caught it in its first LINE.

What the cleanup bought (Yosys, SKY130 hd, ASIC v1 parameters)

ModuleBeforeAfterChange
spi_cmd_rx5,789 µm²5,398 µm²−7 % (no reset on the shift register)
line_renderer8,448 µm²6,790 µm²−20 % (no SETUP state, no own clipper/multiplier)
rect_filler2,355 µm²1,297 µm²−45 % (walks x/y, no address arithmetic)
gpu_core glue2,246 µm²2,754 µm²+23 % (now holds the shared clipper + address)
vga_controller1,346 µm²1,345 µm²same
logic without framebuffer20,184 µm²17,584 µm²−13 %
circle_renderer (new)—10,762 µm²outline + filled circles
frame_buffer (1,200 × 3 bit)141,929 µm²141,929 µm²unchanged

Same speed everywhere: every engine still writes one pixel per clock, and the line engine is one clock faster per command (no SETUP state). And the same pictures: all 111 cube and starburst frames (3 builds) captured from the VGA pins are byte-identical before and after the cleanup.

07

spi_cmd_rx.v — SPI receiver and CDC

readverified

Replaces

The AXI-Lite register bank of your FPGA GPU. The host now speaks SPI instead of the Zynq PS writing registers.

Key decision: SCK is not a clock

If SCK clocked the shift register, the command would live in a second clock domain and handing it to the 25 MHz logic would need a handshake or an async FIFO. Instead the GPU oversamples the three SPI wires with its own clock. Only three single-bit signals cross a clock domain, and a 2-flop synchronizer is exactly the right tool for single bits.

Step by step

  1. Each pin is shifted into a small register every clock: sck_s <= {sck_s[1:0], spi_sck}. Bit [0] may go metastable and has a whole clock (40 ns) to settle before bit [1] samples it.
  2. Only bit [1] (and bit [2] for CS and SCK) is used by logic. sck_rise = sck_s[1] & ~sck_s[2] is one clock long for every SCK rising edge.
  3. MOSI goes through the same two first stages, so mosi_s[1] is exactly the bit that was on the wire when SCK rose.
  4. cs_fall clears bit_count. Each sck_rise with CS low shifts one bit in and counts it (the counter stops at 81, so a long frame stays invalid).
  5. cs_rise with bit_count == 80 copies the shift register to cmd_word and pulses cmd_valid for one clock. Any other count: the frame is ignored.
  6. After reset bit_count starts at 81 ("not in a frame"): if the host was in the middle of a frame when the GPU was reset, the rest of that frame cannot become a command.
PortDirWidthMeaning
clk, resetin125 MHz clock, synchronous reset
spi_cs_n / spi_sck / spi_mosiin1raw SPI pins (asynchronous)
bus_idleout1CS high for two clocks (part of READY)
cmd_validout1one-clock pulse: a complete frame arrived
cmd_wordout80the frame, byte 0 (opcode) in bits 79:72

`timescale 1ns / 1ps

// =============================================================
// spi_cmd_rx : SPI command receiver (mode 0, MSB first, write only)
//
// SCK is never used as a clock. The three SPI pins are sampled by
// the 25 MHz core clock through 2-flop synchronizers and the SCK
// edges are found inside the clk domain, so the whole GPU stays in
// ONE clock domain.  Rule of thumb: f_sck <= f_clk / 8  (~3 MHz).
//
// A frame = CS falls, exactly CMD_BITS rising SCK edges, CS rises.
// Short or long frames are dropped. After reset the receiver waits
// for a CS falling edge, so half a frame can never become a command.
// =============================================================

module spi_cmd_rx #(
    parameter CMD_BITS = 80
)(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire reset,

    // SPI pins (asynchronous to clk)
    input  wire spi_cs_n,
    input  wire spi_sck,
    input  wire spi_mosi,

    output wire bus_idle,                  // CS has been high for 2 clocks
    output reg  cmd_valid,                 // 1-clock pulse: cmd_word is new
    output reg  [CMD_BITS-1:0] cmd_word
);

    localparam CNT_BITS = $clog2(CMD_BITS + 2);
    localparam [CNT_BITS-1:0] FULL = CMD_BITS;       // a complete frame
    localparam [CNT_BITS-1:0] OVER = CMD_BITS + 1;   // too long / not started

    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Synchronizers. Each pin goes through a shift register:
    //   [0] may go metastable, [1] is the clean synchronized value,
    //   [2] is [1] one clock older (for edge detection).
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    (* ASYNC_REG = "TRUE" *) reg [2:0] cs_s;
    (* ASYNC_REG = "TRUE" *) reg [2:0] sck_s;
    (* ASYNC_REG = "TRUE" *) reg [1:0] mosi_s;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            cs_s   <= 3'b111;                // idle: CS high
            sck_s  <= 3'b000;                // idle: SCK low (mode 0)
            mosi_s <= 2'b00;
        end
        else begin
            cs_s   <= {cs_s[1:0],  spi_cs_n};
            sck_s  <= {sck_s[1:0], spi_sck};
            mosi_s <= {mosi_s[0],  spi_mosi};
        end
    end

    wire cs_low   = !cs_s[1];
    wire cs_fall  = !cs_s[1] &&  cs_s[2];
    wire cs_rise  =  cs_s[1] && !cs_s[2];
    wire sck_rise =  sck_s[1] && !sck_s[2];
    wire mosi     =  mosi_s[1];

    assign bus_idle = cs_s[1] && cs_s[2];


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Frame receiver
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    reg [CNT_BITS-1:0] bit_count;
    reg [CMD_BITS-1:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        cmd_valid <= 1'b0;                              // default: no pulse

        if (reset)
            bit_count <= OVER;                          // wait for a CS fall
        else if (cs_fall)
            bit_count <= 0;                             // frame starts
        else if (cs_rise) begin                         // frame ends
            if (bit_count == FULL) begin
                cmd_word  <= shift_reg;
                cmd_valid <= 1'b1;
            end
        end
        else if (cs_low && sck_rise) begin              // one bit
            shift_reg <= {shift_reg[CMD_BITS-2:0], mosi};
            if (bit_count != OVER)                      // saturate: a long
                bit_count <= bit_count + 1'b1;          // frame stays invalid
        end
    end

endmodule
i
Speed limit, explained

The edge detector needs SCK to stay at each level for at least two samples, and MOSI must still be stable two clocks after the SCK edge. With SCK ≤ clk/8 each half-period is ≥ 4 clocks. The sketch uses 2 MHz: 6.25 clocks per half-period.

08

vga_controller.v — VGA timing and scaling

readverified

Same idea as your FPGA version

Two counters walk the 800 × 525 VGA raster; the visible 640 × 480 part reads the framebuffer, the rest produces the sync pulses.

The pieces

  • Scaling: fb_x = h_count >> SCALE_SHIFT, fb_y = v_count >> SCALE_SHIFT. One file serves 320×240 (shift 1), 80×60 (3) and 40×30 (4).
  • Address fb_y · FB_WIDTH + fb_x. FB_WIDTH is a constant, so synthesis builds shifts and adds (for 320 exactly your old (y<<8)+(y<<6)+x, for 40 it is (y<<5)+(y<<3)+x).
  • vblank_start: a one-clock pulse when the counters enter line 480. SWAP waits for it.
  • No reset on the frame contents: frame_valid keeps RGB black until the power-up clear is done.

The two-stage pipeline

ClockWhat happensSignals
tcounters give the screen position → framebuffer addressh_count, v_count, fb_addr
t + 1the framebuffer returns the pixel; visible/sync are delayed by one flop to stay alignedfb_data, visible_d, h_sync_d
t + 2everything is registered on the output pins togetherpixel, hsync, vsync

Registered outputs matter on the ASIC: the pins switch right after the clock edge with almost no logic in front, so the board sees clean edges and the pad delay is predictable.

PortDirWidthMeaning
clk, resetin1pixel clock = system clock
frame_validin1force black until the power-up clear is done
fb_addroutADDR_BITSpixel index into one buffer
fb_datainPIX_BITSpixel, one clock after fb_addr
vblank_startout1pulse at line 480, column 0
hsync, vsync, pixelout1 / 1 / PIX_BITSregistered, 2 clocks after the counters

`timescale 1ns / 1ps

// =============================================================
// vga_controller : 640x480 @ 60 Hz scan-out (25 MHz pixel clock)
//
// The framebuffer is smaller than the screen: every FB pixel is
// repeated (1 << SCALE_SHIFT) times in X and in Y.
//    FPGA : 320 x 240, SCALE_SHIFT = 1   ( 2 x  2 screen pixels)
//    SRAM :  80 x  60, SCALE_SHIFT = 3   ( 8 x  8)
//    ASIC :  40 x  30, SCALE_SHIFT = 4   (16 x 16)
//
// Timing of one pixel (the FB read takes one clock):
//    clock t   : counters -> fb_addr
//    clock t+1 : FB returns fb_data, sync/visible delayed by 1
//    clock t+2 : hsync, vsync, pixel registered on the pins
// =============================================================

module vga_controller #(
    parameter FB_WIDTH    = 320,
    parameter SCALE_SHIFT = 1,
    parameter PIX_BITS    = 8,
    parameter ADDR_BITS   = 17          // >= 11, address of one buffer
)(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire reset,
    input  wire frame_valid,            // black until the FB is cleared

    output wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] fb_addr,   // pixel index into the FB
    input  wire [PIX_BITS-1:0]  fb_data,   // arrives one clock later

    output wire vblank_start,           // 1-clock pulse, first blank line

    output reg  hsync,                  // active low
    output reg  vsync,                  // active low
    output reg  [PIX_BITS-1:0] pixel
);

    // 640x480 @ 60 Hz (VESA): visible, front porch, sync, back porch
    localparam H_VIS = 640, H_FP = 16, H_SYNC = 96, H_BP = 48;
    localparam V_VIS = 480, V_FP = 10, V_SYNC = 2,  V_BP = 33;
    localparam H_TOTAL = H_VIS + H_FP + H_SYNC + H_BP;      // 800
    localparam V_TOTAL = V_VIS + V_FP + V_SYNC + V_BP;      // 525

    reg [9:0] h_count;                  // 0 .. 799
    reg [9:0] v_count;                  // 0 .. 524

    wire visible = (h_count < H_VIS) && (v_count < V_VIS);
    wire h_sync  = (h_count >= H_VIS + H_FP) && (h_count < H_VIS + H_FP + H_SYNC);
    wire v_sync  = (v_count >= V_VIS + V_FP) && (v_count < V_VIS + V_FP + V_SYNC);

    assign vblank_start = (h_count == 0) && (v_count == V_VIS);

    // framebuffer coordinate = screen coordinate / scale
    wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] fb_x = {{(ADDR_BITS-10){1'b0}}, h_count >> SCALE_SHIFT};
    wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] fb_y = {{(ADDR_BITS-10){1'b0}}, v_count >> SCALE_SHIFT};

    // y * FB_WIDTH is a constant multiply: synthesis builds it from
    // shifts and adds (320: (y<<8)+(y<<6), 40: (y<<5)+(y<<3)).
    localparam [ADDR_BITS-1:0] STRIDE = FB_WIDTH[ADDR_BITS-1:0];
    assign fb_addr = visible ? fb_y * STRIDE + fb_x : {ADDR_BITS{1'b0}};

    reg visible_d, h_sync_d, v_sync_d;   // delayed by the FB read latency

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            h_count   <= 0;
            v_count   <= 0;
            visible_d <= 1'b0;
            h_sync_d  <= 1'b0;
            v_sync_d  <= 1'b0;
            hsync     <= 1'b1;
            vsync     <= 1'b1;
            pixel     <= 0;
        end
        else begin
            // counters: h wraps every 800 clocks, v every 525 lines
            if (h_count == H_TOTAL - 1) begin
                h_count <= 0;
                v_count <= (v_count == V_TOTAL - 1) ? 10'd0 : v_count + 1'b1;
            end
            else
                h_count <= h_count + 1'b1;

            // stage 1: wait for the FB data
            visible_d <= visible && frame_valid;
            h_sync_d  <= h_sync;
            v_sync_d  <= v_sync;

            // stage 2: registered outputs, sync pulses are negative
            hsync <= !h_sync_d;
            vsync <= !v_sync_d;
            pixel <= visible_d ? fb_data : {PIX_BITS{1'b0}};
        end
    end

endmodule
09

frame_buffer.v — one write port, one read port

read

Your two-port framebuffer on one clock: the pixel writer uses the write port, the VGA controller the read port, so drawing never has to wait for the display.

  • No initial block. Silicon powers up with random contents; gpu_core clears the memory after every reset instead.
  • Exact depth (DEPTH = W · H · buffers) instead of a power of two. On the FPGA it is BRAM either way; on the ASIC 2,048 words instead of 1,200 would cost 2,544 extra flip-flops.
  • Registered read: data appears one clock after the address — the latency the VGA pipeline is built around, and what BRAM and the SRAM macros give anyway.

// =============================================================
// Frame buffer : 1 write port (draw engines) + 1 read port (VGA)
//
//  FPGA : DEPTH = 2 * 320 * 240 (double buffered), PIX_BITS = 8
//         -> Vivado infers block RAM
//  ASIC : DEPTH = 40 * 30 (single buffer), PIX_BITS = 3
//         -> Yosys builds it out of flip-flops + a read mux
//
// Read data is registered: it appears 1 clock after addr_read.
// No "initial" block on purpose: an ASIC has no power-on contents,
// gpu_core clears the memory after reset instead.
// =============================================================

module frame_buffer #(
    parameter PIX_BITS  = 8,
    parameter DEPTH     = 153600,
    parameter ADDR_BITS = 18
)(
    input wire clk,

    // Write port
    input wire                 write_en,
    input wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] addr_write,
    input wire [PIX_BITS-1:0]  write_data,

    // Read port
    input  wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] addr_read,
    output reg  [PIX_BITS-1:0]  read_data
);

    (* ram_style = "block" *)
    reg [PIX_BITS-1:0] mem [0 : DEPTH-1];

    // Write port
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (write_en)
            mem[addr_write] <= write_data;
    end

    // Read port
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        read_data <= mem[addr_read];
    end

endmodule
i
Read during write

If the VGA reads the address being written in the same clock it gets the old pixel. On screen that is invisible — the next frame shows the new pixel.

line_renderer.v — Bresenham lines, explained

readverified

The problem

A line from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) has to become a chain of pixels: one pixel per step, no gaps, as close to the true line as possible. The obvious way — y = y0 + (x − x0) · slope — needs a division and rounding per pixel. Bresenham's algorithm needs only additions and comparisons, so the hardware is a few adders and the engine can produce one pixel per clock.

The idea: keep score of the error

Walk from the start point towards the end point. At each pixel there are three ways forward: step in x only, in y only, or diagonally (both). Bresenham keeps one integer, err, that says how far the diagonal neighbour is from the true line, and decides from it which way is best:

QuantityValueMeaning
dx|x1 − x0|how far to go in x (≥ 0)
dy−|y1 − y0|how far to go in y, stored negative (≤ 0) — this makes all 8 octants one formula
sx, sy+1 or −1direction of travel in x and y
e(u, v)v · dx + u · dyline equation: 0 exactly on the line (u, v = steps taken in x, y)
erre of the diagonal neighbourstarts as e(1, 1) = dx + dy

Moving in x adds dy to e, moving in y adds dx. Now compare the three candidates. The error of the diagonal is err; of "y only" it is err − dy; of "x only" it is err − dx:

  • Step x (diagonal or x-only) when the diagonal is at least as close as y-only: |err| ≤ |err − dy|. With dy ≤ 0 this works out to err ≥ dy / 2, i.e. 2·err ≥ dy.
  • Step y (diagonal or y-only) when the diagonal is at least as close as x-only: |err| ≤ |err − dx|, i.e. 2·err ≤ dx.
  • Both true → diagonal step. Multiplying by 2 removes the ½, so everything stays integer.
  • After the step, add dy to err for an x-step and dx for a y-step: err is again the error of the new diagonal neighbour.
Bresenham, all octants (the reference model in tb_gpu.v is exactly this)Text

dx  =  |x1 - x0|        sx = (x0 < x1) ? +1 : -1
dy  = -|y1 - y0|        sy = (y0 < y1) ? +1 : -1
err = dx + dy
loop:
    plot(x, y)
    if (x == x1 and y == y1): stop          # end point is drawn too
    e2 = 2 * err
    if (e2 >= dy): err += dy;  x += sx      # step in x
    if (e2 <= dx): err += dx;  y += sy      # step in y

From algorithm to hardware

AlgorithmRTLHardware
dx, dy, err, sx, sy at the startadx_in, ady_in computed straight from the inputs; loaded on start2 subtractors + 2 negators, no extra clock
plot(x, y)plot = busy; x, y are registersevery busy clock is a pixel
the end testat_end = (x == x_end) && (y == y_end)2 comparators; true while the last pixel is plotted
e2 = 2·err{err, 1'b0}just wiring
the two decisionsstep_x = (e2 >= dy_w), step_y = (e2 <= dx_w)2 comparators
err updateerr + add_x + add_yone 3-input adder

Widths and clipping

  • Coordinates are signed 12-bit (−2048 … 2047): a 3D projection often puts an end point off screen. The engine walks the whole line; gpu_core drops the off-screen pixels.
  • dx can be 2047 − (−2048) = 4095 → 13 bits, so the error term uses 14 bits (EW = CW + 2) and e2 one more. Inputs are sign-extended before subtracting so nothing can wrap.
  • Time: max(|dx|, |dy|) + 1 clocks — one per pixel. A full-screen diagonal on the FPGA is 320 clocks = 12.8 µs.

// =============================================================
// line_renderer : Bresenham line, all 8 octants, integer only
//
//   dx  = |x1 - x0|          sx = +1 if x0 < x1 else -1
//   dy  = -|y1 - y0|         sy = +1 if y0 < y1 else -1
//   err = dx + dy
//   loop:  plot(x, y)
//          if (x, y) == (x1, y1): done
//          e2 = 2 * err
//          if e2 >= dy: err += dy, x += sx      (step in x)
//          if e2 <= dx: err += dx, y += sy      (step in y)
//
// One pixel per clock, both end points included. Coordinates are
// signed, so a line may start or end off screen: gpu_core clips
// every pixel, this module only walks the line.
// =============================================================

module line_renderer #(
    parameter CW = 12                   // signed coordinate width
)(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire reset,

    input  wire start,                  // 1-clock pulse, args valid
    input  wire signed [CW-1:0] x0,
    input  wire signed [CW-1:0] y0,
    input  wire signed [CW-1:0] x1,
    input  wire signed [CW-1:0] y1,

    output reg  busy,
    output wire plot,                   // (x, y) is a pixel of the line
    output reg  signed [CW-1:0] x,
    output reg  signed [CW-1:0] y
);

    // |dx|, |dy| need CW+1 bits, their sum one more, plus sign
    localparam EW = CW + 2;

    // ---- set-up values, computed straight from the inputs ----
    // sign-extend first, so x1 - x0 can never overflow
    wire signed [EW-1:0] x0_e = {{2{x0[CW-1]}}, x0};
    wire signed [EW-1:0] x1_e = {{2{x1[CW-1]}}, x1};
    wire signed [EW-1:0] y0_e = {{2{y0[CW-1]}}, y0};
    wire signed [EW-1:0] y1_e = {{2{y1[CW-1]}}, y1};

    wire signed [EW-1:0] dx_in  = x1_e - x0_e;
    wire signed [EW-1:0] dy_in  = y1_e - y0_e;
    wire signed [EW-1:0] adx_in = dx_in[EW-1] ? -dx_in : dx_in;
    wire signed [EW-1:0] ady_in = dy_in[EW-1] ? -dy_in : dy_in;

    // ---- line state ----
    reg signed [EW-1:0] dx;             // +|x1 - x0|
    reg signed [EW-1:0] dy;             // -|y1 - y0|
    reg signed [EW-1:0] err;
    reg                 sx, sy;         // 1 = step +1, 0 = step -1
    reg signed [CW-1:0] x_end, y_end;

    // ---- one Bresenham step ----
    // compare at EW+1 bits. Note: {..} is always UNSIGNED in Verilog,
    // so the extended copies get their own signed wires.
    wire signed [EW:0]  e2     = {err, 1'b0};        // 2 * err
    wire signed [EW:0]  dx_w   = {dx[EW-1], dx};
    wire signed [EW:0]  dy_w   = {dy[EW-1], dy};
    wire                step_x = (e2 >= dy_w);
    wire                step_y = (e2 <= dx_w);
    wire signed [EW-1:0] add_x = step_x ? dy : {EW{1'b0}};
    wire signed [EW-1:0] add_y = step_y ? dx : {EW{1'b0}};
    wire                at_end = (x == x_end) && (y == y_end);

    assign plot = busy;                 // every busy clock is one pixel

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            busy <= 1'b0;

        else if (!busy) begin
            if (start) begin
                busy  <= 1'b1;
                x     <= x0;
                y     <= y0;
                x_end <= x1;
                y_end <= y1;
                dx    <= adx_in;
                dy    <= -ady_in;
                err   <= adx_in - ady_in;
                sx    <= (x0 < x1);
                sy    <= (y0 < y1);
            end
        end

        else if (at_end)
            busy <= 1'b0;               // last pixel was plotted this clock

        else begin
            if (step_x) x <= sx ? x + 1'b1 : x - 1'b1;
            if (step_y) y <= sy ? y + 1'b1 : y - 1'b1;
            err <= err + add_x + add_y;
        end
    end

endmodule

rect_filler.v — rectangles and CLEAR

readverified

The simplest engine: two nested counters. gpu_core has already clipped the rectangle to the screen and turned it into inclusive corners (x0, y0) – (x1, y1), so every clock is a visible pixel and there is no bounds check inside. CLEAR is the full-screen rectangle (0, 0) – (W−1, H−1).

Step by step

  1. On start: x ← x0, y ← y0, remember x0 (start of every row), x1 and y1.
  2. Every busy clock plots (x, y). If x ≠ x1: x ← x + 1.
  3. Else, if y ≠ y1: next row — x ← x0, y ← y + 1.
  4. Else (x1, y1) was the last pixel: busy ← 0.
Clockxyaddress y·40 + xnext
136243x+1
246244x+1
356245x+1
466246row end → x = 3, y = 7
537283x+1
……
867286done
i
Where did the address arithmetic go?

Your FPGA rect.v avoided the multiply by stepping the address (+1 per pixel, +stride per row). Now the address y · W + x is computed once in gpu_core for all engines; W is a constant, so it is two adders (320 = 256 + 64), not a multiplier. The rectangle engine shrank from 2,355 to 1,297 µm².

// =============================================================
// rect_filler : filled rectangle, one pixel per clock
//
// Walks x from x0 to x1, then the next row, until (x1, y1).
// The corners are inclusive and already clipped to the screen by
// gpu_core (0 <= x0 <= x1 < W, 0 <= y0 <= y1 < H), so every clock
// is a visible pixel. CLEAR is a full-screen rectangle.
// =============================================================

module rect_filler #(
    parameter XW = 9,                   // x bits (320 -> 9)
    parameter YW = 8                    // y bits (240 -> 8)
)(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire reset,

    input  wire start,                  // 1-clock pulse, args valid
    input  wire [XW-1:0] x0,
    input  wire [YW-1:0] y0,
    input  wire [XW-1:0] x1,
    input  wire [YW-1:0] y1,

    output reg  busy,
    output wire plot,
    output reg  [XW-1:0] x,
    output reg  [YW-1:0] y
);

    reg [XW-1:0] x_first, x_last;
    reg [YW-1:0] y_last;

    assign plot = busy;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            busy <= 1'b0;

        else if (!busy) begin
            if (start) begin
                busy    <= 1'b1;
                x       <= x0;
                y       <= y0;
                x_first <= x0;
                x_last  <= x1;
                y_last  <= y1;
            end
        end

        else if (x != x_last)
            x <= x + 1'b1;              // next pixel in the row

        else if (y != y_last) begin
            x <= x_first;               // next row
            y <= y + 1'b1;
        end

        else
            busy <= 1'b0;               // (x1, y1) was the last pixel
    end

endmodule

circle_renderer.v — midpoint circles, outline and filled

readverified

What it draws

New command 0x05 CIRCLE: A = cx, B = cy, C = r (0 … 2047), D bit 0 = fill (0 = outline, 1 = filled disc). Like the line, the centre may be anywhere — even off screen — and everything is clipped. The algorithm is the midpoint circle algorithm (Bresenham's circle): again only additions, subtractions and comparisons — no multiplier, no square root, no sine table.

Idea 1: compute one eighth, mirror the rest

A circle is symmetric about the x axis, the y axis and both diagonals. If (x, y) is on a circle around the origin, so are (±x, ±y) and (±y, ±x) — eight points. So the engine only walks octant 0: from (r, 0) at 3 o'clock down to the 45° diagonal where x = y. Every point it finds there gives eight pixels.

Idea 2: walk the octant with a midpoint test

In octant 0 the circle is steep: every step goes one row further (y + 1), and x either stays or moves one column inwards (x − 1). To choose, look at the point exactly halfway between the two candidates and ask whether it is inside or outside the circle. With f(x, y) = x² + y² − r² (negative inside, positive outside):

Why there are no squares in the hardware

d is never computed from scratch. When y grows by one and x maybe shrinks by one, the change of d is simple (y′, x′ are the new values):

ChoiceNew midpointd′ − dUpdate in the RTL
A: x stays (d < 0)(x − ½, y′ + 1)(y′+1)² − y′² = 2·y′ + 1d + 2·y_n + 1
B: x − 1 (d ≥ 0)(x′ − ½, y′ + 1)2·y′ + 1 − 2·x′d + 2·(y_n − x_n) + 1

The RTL writes both as d + (inc <<< 1) + 1 with inc = d_neg ? y_n : y_n − x_n: one subtractor, one multiplexer, a shift (wiring) and one adder.

Start value. The first midpoint is (r − ½, 1): f = (r − ½)² + 1 − r² = 5/4 − r. Every update adds an integer, so the true d is always "integer + ¼". For the sign test the ¼ never matters (an integer n satisfies n + ¼ < 0 exactly when n < 0), so the hardware starts at d = 1 − r and stays integer. Stop: when the next point would have x < y, the octant is finished (signal last).

midpoint circle, octant 0 (circle_renderer.v and the testbench model do exactly this)Text
1
2
3
4
5
6
7
8
x = r, y = 0, d = 1 - r
loop:
    draw step (x, y)                    # 8 points, or up to 4 spans
    y' = y + 1
    if d < 0:  x' = x,     d' = d + 2*y' + 1
    else:      x' = x - 1, d' = d + 2*(y' - x') + 1
    if x' < y': stop                     # "last"
    x, y, d = x', y', d'

Worked example: r = 7

Step(x, y)dd < 0 ?next (x′, y′)d′last?
1(7,0)-6yes(7,1)-6 + 2·1 + 1 = -3no
2(7,1)-3yes(7,2)-3 + 2·2 + 1 = 2no
3(7,2)2no(6,3)2 + 2·(3−6) + 1 = -3no
4(6,3)-3yes(6,4)-3 + 2·4 + 1 = 6no
5(6,4)6no(5,5)6 + 2·(5−5) + 1 = 7no
6(5,5)7no(4,6)—yes → done

Outline: 8 pixels per step

A 3-bit counter k runs 0…7; a case statement turns it into the offset (ox, oy) — the table in the symmetry picture. px = cx + ox, py = cy + oy. After k = 7 the engine takes the next step. On the first step (y = 0) and on the diagonal (x = y) some of the eight points coincide; they are simply written twice — skipping them would need more logic than it saves (at most 8 extra clocks per circle).

Filled: spans, each row exactly once

The same walk gives the horizontal extent of the disc: row cy ± y goes from cx − x to cx + x, and row cy ± x from cx − y to cx + y. Drawing all four spans at every step would draw many rows again and again, because x often stays the same for several steps. The rules that make every row appear exactly once:

Span sRowFrom … toDrawn when
0cy + ycx − x … cx + xevery step
1cy − ycx − x … cx + xevery step except y = 0 (that row is span 0)
2cy + xcx − y … cx + yonly on the last step before x changes (d ≥ 0) or the very last step — that is the widest span this row gets — and not when x = y (same row as span 0)
3cy − xcx − y … cx + ysame as span 2
✓
Checked for every radius from 0 to 400

scripts/check_circle.py (in the zip, independent of the RTL) checks that every outline pixel lies within half a pixel of the true circle, the outline has no gaps, the filled disc writes no pixel twice, and the filled disc is exactly every row filled between the leftmost and rightmost outline pixel — so a filled circle and its outline always match. Result: ALL CHECKS PASSED. The testbench then checks the RTL against the same rules pixel by pixel.

Clipping without wasting clocks

Each span is clipped to the screen before it is walked (left_c, rght_c, row inside 0…H−1). A span that is completely off screen costs one clock (S_SPAN_SET) instead of hundreds. gpu_core still checks every pixel, so even a wrong clip here could never write outside the framebuffer.

Widths

  • r is 11 bits (0…2047). cx ± r can reach ±4095, so positions use PW = 15 bits signed (COORD_BITS + 3), comfortably holding d too (|d| ≤ about 3·r).
  • The extreme case CIRCLE (2047, −2048, r = 2047) is in the testbench: it must write nothing (all off screen) and must finish.

// =============================================================
// circle_renderer : midpoint (Bresenham) circle, outline or filled
//
// Walks one octant (from (r, 0) up to the 45 degree diagonal) and
// uses the 8-way symmetry of the circle for the rest:
//
//   x = r, y = 0, d = 1 - r
//   while x >= y:
//       draw step (x, y)                       <- 8 points or 4 spans
//       y = y + 1
//       if d < 0:  d = d + 2*y + 1             (stay on this column)
//       else:      x = x - 1
//                  d = d + 2*(y - x) + 1       (step inwards)
//
// OUTLINE : 8 pixels per step, one per clock
//           (cx+-x, cy+-y) and (cx+-y, cy+-x)
// FILLED  : up to 4 horizontal spans per step
//           rows cy+-y from cx-x to cx+x      (every step)
//           rows cy+-x from cx-y to cx+y      (only on the last step
//                                              before x changes, so
//                                              each row is drawn once)
//           Spans are clipped to the screen before they are walked,
//           so off-screen parts cost no clocks.
//
// Only adds, subtracts and compares: no multiplier, no square root.
// gpu_core clips every pixel again, so nothing can be written
// outside the framebuffer whatever cx, cy and r are.
// =============================================================

module circle_renderer #(
    parameter CW       = 15,            // signed width of cx, cy, x, y, d
    parameter RW       = 11,            // radius bits (0 .. 2047)
    parameter SCREEN_W = 320,
    parameter SCREEN_H = 240
)(
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire reset,

    input  wire start,                  // 1-clock pulse, args valid
    input  wire fill,                   // 0 = outline, 1 = filled disc
    input  wire signed [CW-1:0] cx_in,
    input  wire signed [CW-1:0] cy_in,
    input  wire [RW-1:0]        r_in,

    output reg  busy,
    output wire plot,
    output wire signed [CW-1:0] px,
    output wire signed [CW-1:0] py
);

    localparam signed [CW-1:0] ONE  = 1;
    localparam signed [CW-1:0] ZERO = 0;
    localparam X_LAST = SCREEN_W - 1;
    localparam Y_LAST = SCREEN_H - 1;
    localparam signed [CW-1:0] XMAX = X_LAST[CW-1:0];
    localparam signed [CW-1:0] YMAX = Y_LAST[CW-1:0];

    localparam [1:0] S_POINTS   = 2'd0;  // outline: 8 points per step
    localparam [1:0] S_SPAN_SET = 2'd1;  // filled: choose + clip a span
    localparam [1:0] S_SPAN_RUN = 2'd2;  // filled: walk the span

    reg [1:0] state;
    reg signed [CW-1:0] cx, cy;          // centre
    reg signed [CW-1:0] x, y, d;         // octant position + decision
    reg [2:0] k;                         // outline: which of the 8 points
    reg [1:0] s;                         // filled:  which of the 4 spans
    reg signed [CW-1:0] run_x, run_end, run_row;   // span being walked


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Next midpoint step (used by both modes)
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    wire                 d_neg = d[CW-1];             // d < 0
    wire signed [CW-1:0] y_n   = y + ONE;
    wire signed [CW-1:0] x_n   = d_neg ? x : x - ONE;
    wire signed [CW-1:0] inc   = d_neg ? y_n : y_n - x_n;
    wire signed [CW-1:0] d_n   = d + (inc <<< 1) + ONE;
    wire                 last  = (x_n < y_n);         // octant finished


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // OUTLINE: point k of the 8 symmetric points
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    reg signed [CW-1:0] ox, oy;          // offset from the centre

    always @(*) begin
        case (k)
            3'd0:    begin ox =  x; oy =  y; end
            3'd1:    begin ox =  y; oy =  x; end
            3'd2:    begin ox = -y; oy =  x; end
            3'd3:    begin ox = -x; oy =  y; end
            3'd4:    begin ox = -x; oy = -y; end
            3'd5:    begin ox = -y; oy = -x; end
            3'd6:    begin ox =  y; oy = -x; end
            default: begin ox =  x; oy = -y; end
        endcase
    end


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // FILLED: span s of the current step
    //   s = 0 : row cy + y, half width x      s = 2 : row cy + x, half width y
    //   s = 1 : row cy - y, half width x      s = 3 : row cy - x, half width y
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    wire signed [CW-1:0] row_off = s[1] ? x : y;
    wire signed [CW-1:0] half    = s[1] ? y : x;
    wire signed [CW-1:0] row     = s[0] ? cy - row_off : cy + row_off;

    // which spans are needed in this step (each row exactly once)
    wire span_on = s[1] ? ((!d_neg || last) && (x != y))   // x rows: widest span only
                        : (!s[0] || (y != ZERO));          // y rows: row cy-0 = cy+0

    // clip the span to the screen
    wire signed [CW-1:0] left   = cx - half;
    wire signed [CW-1:0] right  = cx + half;
    wire signed [CW-1:0] left_c = (left  < ZERO) ? ZERO : left;
    wire signed [CW-1:0] rght_c = (right > XMAX) ? XMAX : right;

    wire span_visible = span_on && (row >= ZERO) && (row <= YMAX) && (left_c <= rght_c);


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Control
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    wire span_done = (state == S_SPAN_SET && !span_visible) ||
                     (state == S_SPAN_RUN && run_x == run_end);

    // advance (x, y, d) after the 8th point or after the 4th span
    wire step = (state == S_POINTS) ? (k == 3'd7) : (span_done && s == 2'd3);

    assign plot = busy && (state == S_POINTS || state == S_SPAN_RUN);
    assign px   = (state == S_POINTS) ? cx + ox : run_x;
    assign py   = (state == S_POINTS) ? cy + oy : run_row;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            busy <= 1'b0;

        else if (!busy) begin
            if (start) begin
                busy  <= 1'b1;
                state <= fill ? S_SPAN_SET : S_POINTS;
                cx    <= cx_in;
                cy    <= cy_in;
                x     <= $signed({{(CW-RW){1'b0}}, r_in});
                y     <= ZERO;
                d     <= ONE - $signed({{(CW-RW){1'b0}}, r_in});
                k     <= 3'd0;
                s     <= 2'd0;
            end
        end

        else begin
            case (state)
                S_POINTS:
                    k <= k + 1'b1;                      // wraps 7 -> 0

                S_SPAN_SET:
                    if (span_visible) begin
                        run_x   <= left_c;
                        run_end <= rght_c;
                        run_row <= row;
                        state   <= S_SPAN_RUN;
                    end

                default:                                // S_SPAN_RUN
                    if (run_x != run_end)
                        run_x <= run_x + ONE;
                    else
                        state <= S_SPAN_SET;
            endcase

            if (span_done)
                s <= s + 1'b1;                          // wraps 3 -> 0

            if (step) begin
                x <= x_n;
                y <= y_n;
                d <= d_n;
                if (last)
                    busy <= 1'b0;
            end
        end
    end

endmodule
13

gpu_core.v — decode, pixel writer, reset, double buffering

readverified

gpu_core takes the role of your vga_top.v without the Zynq PS, AXI, 3D pipeline, textures and depth buffer. Read it top to bottom; each block is one idea:

  1. Reset synchronizer — a 2-bit shift register: rst_n low sets it at once (asynchronously), release happens on a clock edge two clocks later. Everything else uses the clean synchronous reset.
  2. Power-up clear — init_addr walks the whole memory writing 0, one word per clock. RGB is forced black and READY is low until init_done.
  3. Command fields — the 80-bit word is cut into op, A, B, C, D and the colour; only the low 12 bits of each argument are used.
  4. Accept — a command is accepted only when nothing is busy (idle); a command sent while busy is dropped. gpu_ready = idle & !cmd_valid & bus_idle. The colour is latched once per command into draw_color.
  5. RECT clipping — inclusive corners x0 = x, x1 = x + w − 1 in 14-bit signed, clamped to 0 … W−1 (same for y). If x0 > x1 or y0 > y1 the rectangle is invisible (this also covers w = 0 and h = 0) and the engine is never started. CLEAR feeds the full-screen corners.
  6. Engines — one start pulse each; the circle gets its centre sign-extended to 15 bits and fill = D[0].
  7. Pixel writer — choose the plotting engine, widen to 15-bit signed, keep only 0 ≤ x < W and 0 ≤ y < H, address = back buffer + y · W + x.
  8. SWAP / double buffering — drawing always targets the back buffer. SWAP sets swap_pending; at vblank_start the buffers flip. With DOUBLE_BUF = 0 SWAP only waits for vblank (used by the ASIC sketch to start drawing during blanking).
  9. Framebuffer + VGA — the init sweep owns the write port until done; the VGA reads the front buffer.

How one command travels through the core

ClockWhat happensSignal to watch
hostCS rises after 80 SCK edgesspi_cs_n
+2CS has passed the synchronizeru_spi.cs_s[1]
+3rising edge seen, 80 bits → cmd_valid = 1 for one clock; READY dropscmd_valid, gpu_ready
+3accept = cmd_valid & idle → one engine gets start; the colour is latchedaccept, u_*.start
+4 …engine busy, one pixel per clock: plot → clip → address → writeplot, fb_we, fb_waddr
endbusy = 0 → READY = 1 → the host may send the next commandgpu_ready
ParameterFPGAASIC v1ASIC v2Effect
FB_W × FB_H320 × 24040 × 3080 × 60framebuffer size
SCALE_SHIFT143screen px per FB px = 2^shift
PIX_BITS838RGB332 or RGB111
DOUBLE_BUF100second buffer + flip at vblank
COORD_BITS121212signed coordinate range ±2047
i
On the FPGA you build this core in three steps

Part 3 does not start with this file. It brings the GPU up the way you would write it: bringup/step2_rect/gpu_core.v (RECT only, no clipping in the writer), then bringup/step3_line/gpu_core.v (+ LINE and the clipping writer), then this file (+ CIRCLE, 15-bit writer). Each step shows the exact diff and has its own tests on the monitor.

// =============================================================
// gpu_core : SPI rasterizer GPU
//            VGA scan-out + framebuffer + line + rectangle + circle
//
// The SAME file is used on the PYNQ-Z2 and in the SKY130 ASIC,
// only the parameters change:
//
//   parameter     FPGA (PYNQ-Z2)   ASIC v1 (SKY130)   ASIC v2 (SRAM)
//   FB_W x FB_H   320 x 240        40 x 30            80 x 60
//   SCALE_SHIFT   1  (2 x 2)       4  (16 x 16)       3  (8 x 8)
//   PIX_BITS      8  (RGB332)      3  (RGB111)        8
//   DOUBLE_BUF    1                0                  0
//
// This is the complete core (bring-up step 4). The FPGA bring-up builds
// it up in steps: bringup/step2_rect/gpu_core.v (RECT only), then
// bringup/step3_line/gpu_core.v (+ LINE), then this file (+ CIRCLE).
//
// Host protocol: one 10-byte SPI frame per command (mode 0, MSB
// first, CS low for the whole frame). Wait for gpu_ready = 1
// before every frame.
//
//   byte 0      opcode
//   byte 1..2   A  (int16, big endian)
//   byte 3..4   B
//   byte 5..6   C
//   byte 7..8   D
//   byte 9      colour, RGB332 (RRRGGGBB)
//
//   0x01 CLEAR   -                       fill the whole back buffer
//   0x02 LINE    A=x0 B=y0 C=x1 D=y1     Bresenham, both ends drawn
//   0x03 RECT    A=x  B=y  C=w  D=h      filled
//   0x04 SWAP    -                       show the back buffer at the
//                                        next vblank (single buffer:
//                                        just wait for vblank)
//   0x05 CIRCLE  A=cx B=cy C=r  D=fill   midpoint circle, D bit 0:
//                                        0 = outline, 1 = filled
//
// Coordinates use the low COORD_BITS bits as a signed number
// (-2048 .. 2047), w/h the low COORD_BITS bits unsigned, r the low
// COORD_BITS-1 bits (0 .. 2047). Anything off screen is clipped.
// =============================================================

module gpu_core #(
    parameter FB_W        = 320,
    parameter FB_H        = 240,
    parameter SCALE_SHIFT = 1,
    parameter PIX_BITS    = 8,
    parameter DOUBLE_BUF  = 1,
    parameter COORD_BITS  = 12
)(
    input  wire clk,                    // 25 MHz pixel + system clock
    input  wire rst_n,                  // asynchronous, active low

    input  wire spi_cs_n,               // SPI from the host MCU
    input  wire spi_sck,
    input  wire spi_mosi,
    output wire gpu_ready,

    output wire vga_hs,
    output wire vga_vs,
    output wire [PIX_BITS-1:0] vga_pix,

    output reg  dbg_cmd_toggle          // LED on the FPGA, unused on the ASIC
);

    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Sizes
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    localparam FB_PIXELS = FB_W * FB_H;
    localparam DEPTH     = DOUBLE_BUF ? 2 * FB_PIXELS : FB_PIXELS;
    localparam ADDR_BITS = $clog2(DEPTH);
    localparam XW        = $clog2(FB_W);          // bits of an on-screen x
    localparam YW        = $clog2(FB_H);
    localparam CB        = COORD_BITS;
    localparam PW        = COORD_BITS + 3;        // pixel coordinate width
                                                  // (circle: cx +- r)

    localparam [7:0] OP_CLEAR  = 8'h01;
    localparam [7:0] OP_LINE   = 8'h02;
    localparam [7:0] OP_RECT   = 8'h03;
    localparam [7:0] OP_SWAP   = 8'h04;
    localparam [7:0] OP_CIRCLE = 8'h05;


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Reset synchronizer: assert at once, release on a clock edge
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    (* ASYNC_REG = "TRUE" *) reg [1:0] reset_s;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n)
            reset_s <= 2'b11;
        else
            reset_s <= {reset_s[0], 1'b0};
    end

    wire reset = reset_s[1];


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Power-up clear: write 0 to every word once after reset
    // (silicon has no initial values)
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    localparam LAST_I = DEPTH - 1;
    localparam [ADDR_BITS-1:0] LAST_ADDR = LAST_I[ADDR_BITS-1:0];

    reg                 init_done;
    reg [ADDR_BITS-1:0] init_addr;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            init_done <= 1'b0;
            init_addr <= 0;
        end
        else if (!init_done) begin
            if (init_addr == LAST_ADDR)
                init_done <= 1'b1;
            else
                init_addr <= init_addr + 1'b1;
        end
    end


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // SPI receiver
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    wire        bus_idle;
    wire        cmd_valid;
    wire [79:0] cmd_word;

    spi_cmd_rx #(.CMD_BITS(80)) u_spi (
        .clk(clk), .reset(reset),
        .spi_cs_n(spi_cs_n), .spi_sck(spi_sck), .spi_mosi(spi_mosi),
        .bus_idle(bus_idle), .cmd_valid(cmd_valid), .cmd_word(cmd_word)
    );


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Command fields
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // The protocol carries int16 values; only the low bits are used.
    /* verilator lint_off UNUSEDSIGNAL */
    wire [7:0]  op     = cmd_word[79:72];
    wire [15:0] arg_a  = cmd_word[71:56];
    wire [15:0] arg_b  = cmd_word[55:40];
    wire [15:0] arg_c  = cmd_word[39:24];
    wire [15:0] arg_d  = cmd_word[23:8];
    wire [7:0]  rgb332 = cmd_word[7:0];
    /* verilator lint_on UNUSEDSIGNAL */

    wire signed [CB-1:0] a = arg_a[CB-1:0];
    wire signed [CB-1:0] b = arg_b[CB-1:0];
    wire signed [CB-1:0] c = arg_c[CB-1:0];
    wire signed [CB-1:0] d = arg_d[CB-1:0];

    // RGB332 -> framebuffer pixel (ASIC: keep the MSB of R, G and B)
    wire [PIX_BITS-1:0] cmd_color;
    generate
        if (PIX_BITS == 3) begin : g_rgb111
            assign cmd_color = {rgb332[7], rgb332[4], rgb332[1]};
        end
        else begin : g_rgb332
            assign cmd_color = rgb332[PIX_BITS-1:0];
        end
    endgenerate


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Accepting a command
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    wire line_busy, rect_busy, circ_busy;
    reg  swap_pending;

    wire idle   = init_done && !line_busy && !rect_busy && !circ_busy && !swap_pending;
    wire accept = cmd_valid && idle;      // a command sent while busy is dropped

    assign gpu_ready = idle && !cmd_valid && bus_idle;

    wire is_clear  = (op == OP_CLEAR);
    wire is_line   = (op == OP_LINE);
    wire is_rect   = (op == OP_RECT);
    wire is_swap   = (op == OP_SWAP);
    wire is_circle = (op == OP_CIRCLE);

    // colour for the whole command, latched once
    reg [PIX_BITS-1:0] draw_color;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            dbg_cmd_toggle <= 1'b0;
        else if (accept) begin
            dbg_cmd_toggle <= !dbg_cmd_toggle;
            draw_color     <= cmd_color;
        end
    end


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // RECT / CLEAR: clip [x, x+w) x [y, y+h) to the screen.
    // The filler then only walks visible pixels.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    localparam BW = CB + 2;                         // holds x + w

    localparam X_LAST = FB_W - 1;
    localparam Y_LAST = FB_H - 1;
    localparam signed [BW-1:0] B_ONE  = 1;
    localparam signed [BW-1:0] B_ZERO = 0;
    localparam signed [BW-1:0] B_XMAX = X_LAST[BW-1:0];
    localparam signed [BW-1:0] B_YMAX = Y_LAST[BW-1:0];

    wire signed [BW-1:0] rx0 = {{2{a[CB-1]}}, a};   // sign-extended
    wire signed [BW-1:0] ry0 = {{2{b[CB-1]}}, b};
    wire signed [BW-1:0] rx1 = rx0 + $signed({2'b00, arg_c[CB-1:0]}) - B_ONE;   // inclusive
    wire signed [BW-1:0] ry1 = ry0 + $signed({2'b00, arg_d[CB-1:0]}) - B_ONE;

    wire signed [BW-1:0] kx0 = (rx0 < B_ZERO) ? B_ZERO : rx0;
    wire signed [BW-1:0] ky0 = (ry0 < B_ZERO) ? B_ZERO : ry0;
    wire signed [BW-1:0] kx1 = (rx1 > B_XMAX) ? B_XMAX : rx1;
    wire signed [BW-1:0] ky1 = (ry1 > B_YMAX) ? B_YMAX : ry1;

    // w = 0 or h = 0 or completely off screen -> nothing to draw
    wire rect_visible = (kx0 <= kx1) && (ky0 <= ky1);

    /* verilator lint_off UNUSEDSIGNAL */
    wire [XW-1:0] fill_x0 = is_clear ? {XW{1'b0}} : kx0[XW-1:0];
    wire [YW-1:0] fill_y0 = is_clear ? {YW{1'b0}} : ky0[YW-1:0];
    wire [XW-1:0] fill_x1 = is_clear ? B_XMAX[XW-1:0] : kx1[XW-1:0];
    wire [YW-1:0] fill_y1 = is_clear ? B_YMAX[YW-1:0] : ky1[YW-1:0];
    /* verilator lint_on UNUSEDSIGNAL */


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Draw engines. Each one only says "plot (x, y)", one pixel
    // per clock. Exactly one engine is busy at a time.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    wire                 line_plot, rect_plot, circ_plot;
    wire signed [CB-1:0] line_x, line_y;
    wire [XW-1:0]        rect_x;
    wire [YW-1:0]        rect_y;
    wire signed [PW-1:0] circ_x, circ_y;

    line_renderer #(.CW(CB)) u_line (
        .clk(clk), .reset(reset),
        .start(accept && is_line),
        .x0(a), .y0(b), .x1(c), .y1(d),
        .busy(line_busy), .plot(line_plot), .x(line_x), .y(line_y)
    );

    rect_filler #(.XW(XW), .YW(YW)) u_rect (
        .clk(clk), .reset(reset),
        .start(accept && (is_clear || (is_rect && rect_visible))),
        .x0(fill_x0), .y0(fill_y0), .x1(fill_x1), .y1(fill_y1),
        .busy(rect_busy), .plot(rect_plot), .x(rect_x), .y(rect_y)
    );

    wire signed [PW-1:0] cx_p = {{3{a[CB-1]}}, a};  // sign-extend to PW
    wire signed [PW-1:0] cy_p = {{3{b[CB-1]}}, b};

    circle_renderer #(.CW(PW), .RW(CB - 1), .SCREEN_W(FB_W), .SCREEN_H(FB_H)) u_circ (
        .clk(clk), .reset(reset),
        .start(accept && is_circle),
        .fill(arg_d[0]),
        .cx_in(cx_p), .cy_in(cy_p),
        .r_in(arg_c[CB-2:0]),
        .busy(circ_busy), .plot(circ_plot), .px(circ_x), .py(circ_y)
    );


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Pixel writer, shared by all engines:
    //   pick the active engine -> clip -> address = y * FB_W + x
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    localparam signed [PW-1:0] P_ZERO = 0;
    localparam signed [PW-1:0] P_W    = FB_W[PW-1:0];
    localparam signed [PW-1:0] P_H    = FB_H[PW-1:0];

    wire signed [PW-1:0] rect_xs = $signed({{(PW-XW){1'b0}}, rect_x});
    wire signed [PW-1:0] rect_ys = $signed({{(PW-YW){1'b0}}, rect_y});

    wire signed [PW-1:0] line_xs = {{3{line_x[CB-1]}}, line_x};
    wire signed [PW-1:0] line_ys = {{3{line_y[CB-1]}}, line_y};

    wire                 plot    = line_plot || rect_plot || circ_plot;
    wire signed [PW-1:0] plot_x  = line_plot ? line_xs : circ_plot ? circ_x : rect_xs;
    wire signed [PW-1:0] plot_y  = line_plot ? line_ys : circ_plot ? circ_y : rect_ys;

    wire on_screen = (plot_x >= P_ZERO) && (plot_x < P_W) &&
                     (plot_y >= P_ZERO) && (plot_y < P_H);

    wire draw_we = plot && on_screen;

    // only used when on_screen, so the low XW / YW bits are the whole value
    localparam [ADDR_BITS-1:0] STRIDE = FB_W[ADDR_BITS-1:0];
    wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] draw_x = {{(ADDR_BITS-XW){1'b0}}, plot_x[XW-1:0]};
    wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] draw_y = {{(ADDR_BITS-YW){1'b0}}, plot_y[YW-1:0]};


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // SWAP and double buffering
    //   front_buf = the buffer on screen; we always draw the other one
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    reg  front_buf;
    wire vblank_start;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            front_buf    <= 1'b0;
            swap_pending <= 1'b0;
        end
        else if (accept && is_swap)
            swap_pending <= 1'b1;
        else if (swap_pending && vblank_start) begin
            swap_pending <= 1'b0;
            if (DOUBLE_BUF)
                front_buf <= !front_buf;
        end
    end

    localparam BUF1_I = DOUBLE_BUF ? FB_PIXELS : 0;
    localparam [ADDR_BITS-1:0] BUF1 = BUF1_I[ADDR_BITS-1:0];
    wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] front_base = front_buf ? BUF1 : {ADDR_BITS{1'b0}};
    wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] back_base  = front_buf ? {ADDR_BITS{1'b0}} : BUF1;


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Framebuffer: the init sweep has the write port until done
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    wire                 fb_we    = (!init_done && !reset) || draw_we;
    wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] fb_waddr = init_done ? back_base + draw_y * STRIDE + draw_x : init_addr;
    wire [PIX_BITS-1:0]  fb_wdata = init_done ? draw_color : {PIX_BITS{1'b0}};

    wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] scan_addr;
    wire [PIX_BITS-1:0]  scan_data;

    frame_buffer #(.PIX_BITS(PIX_BITS), .DEPTH(DEPTH), .ADDR_BITS(ADDR_BITS)) u_fb (
        .clk(clk),
        .write_en(fb_we), .addr_write(fb_waddr), .write_data(fb_wdata),
        .addr_read(front_base + scan_addr), .read_data(scan_data)
    );


    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // VGA scan-out
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    vga_controller #(
        .FB_WIDTH(FB_W), .SCALE_SHIFT(SCALE_SHIFT),
        .PIX_BITS(PIX_BITS), .ADDR_BITS(ADDR_BITS)
    ) u_vga (
        .clk(clk), .reset(reset), .frame_valid(init_done),
        .fb_addr(scan_addr), .fb_data(scan_data),
        .vblank_start(vblank_start),
        .hsync(vga_hs), .vsync(vga_vs), .pixel(vga_pix)
    );

endmodule
02

Simulate before you touch hardware

Run everything in the LibreLane devshell (it ships Icarus Verilog 13). One script runs all of it in about a minute.

14

The self-checking testbench

WSLdevshellverified

How it checks

sim/tb_gpu.v keeps a software model of the framebuffer. After every command it checks the number of pixels written and compares every pixel of the back buffer; then it captures a whole VGA frame from the output pins and checks all 800 × 525 samples including HSYNC and VSYNC.

GroupWhat is tested
[1]READY and RGB low during reset; exact count of power-up clear writes
[2]lines: 8 octants, horizontal, vertical, single point, clipped at both ends, fully off screen
[3]rectangles: normal, clipped top-left (negative x/y), clipped bottom-right, zero width, off screen
[4]circles: outline + filled, r = 0 and 1, clipped on every side, off screen, r bigger than the screen, the extreme (2047, −2048, 2047)
[5]79-bit frame, 81-bit frame, unknown opcode → nothing written
[6]a second command sent while CLEAR is busy → dropped
[7]scene with lines, rectangles and circles + SWAP; the swap must land exactly on vblank; full frame from the pins
[8]reset in the middle of a command → clean restart

The model is written the simple way (loops over integers, no widths, no FSMs), so a mistake in the RTL's bit widths or state machine shows up as a mismatch. For the circle it uses the same span rules as the RTL — and scripts/check_circle.py separately proves those rules give the right disc.

`timescale 1ns / 1ps

// =============================================================
// Self-checking testbench for gpu_core
//   [1] reset + power-up clear   [5] malformed SPI frames
//   [2] lines                    [6] command while busy
//   [3] rectangles               [7] SWAP + full frame from the pins
//   [4] circles                  [8] reset in the middle of a command
//
//   default        : FPGA parameters (320x240, RGB332, double buffer)
//   -DASIC_CFG     : ASIC parameters (40x30,  RGB111, single buffer)
//
//   +vcd                     dump waveforms to build/gpu.vcd
//   +demo=<file.hex>         run a command stream from gen_demo.py
//   +frames=<prefix>         where captured VGA frames are written
//
// A software model of the framebuffer is kept next to the DUT.
// After every command the DUT memory is compared with the model,
// and captured VGA frames are compared pixel-by-pixel too.
// =============================================================

module tb_gpu;

`ifdef ASIC_CFG
    localparam FB_W = 40,  FB_H = 30,  SHIFT = 4, PIX_BITS = 3, DOUBLE_BUF = 0;
`elsif SRAM_CFG
    localparam FB_W = 80,  FB_H = 60,  SHIFT = 3, PIX_BITS = 8, DOUBLE_BUF = 0;
`else
    localparam FB_W = 320, FB_H = 240, SHIFT = 1, PIX_BITS = 8, DOUBLE_BUF = 1;
`endif
    localparam FB_PIXELS = FB_W * FB_H;
    localparam DEPTH     = FB_PIXELS * (DOUBLE_BUF ? 2 : 1);
    localparam SPI_HALF  = 250;               // 2 MHz SCK

    // ---------------- clock / DUT ----------------
    reg clk = 1'b0;
    always #20 clk = ~clk;                    // 25 MHz

    reg rst_n = 1'b0;
    reg cs_n  = 1'b1, sck = 1'b0, mosi = 1'b0;
    wire ready, hs, vs, dbg;
    wire [PIX_BITS-1:0] pix;

    gpu_core #(
        .FB_W(FB_W), .FB_H(FB_H), .SCALE_SHIFT(SHIFT),
        .PIX_BITS(PIX_BITS), .DOUBLE_BUF(DOUBLE_BUF)
    ) dut (
        .clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n),
        .spi_cs_n(cs_n), .spi_sck(sck), .spi_mosi(mosi),
        .gpu_ready(ready),
        .vga_hs(hs), .vga_vs(vs), .vga_pix(pix),
        .dbg_cmd_toggle(dbg)
    );

    // ---------------- write monitor ----------------
    integer writes = 0;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (dut.fb_we === 1'b1) begin
            if (dut.fb_waddr >= DEPTH)
                $fatal(1, "FB write out of range: %0d", dut.fb_waddr);
            if (dut.line_plot + dut.rect_plot + dut.circ_plot > 1)
                $fatal(1, "two engines plotting at once");
            writes = writes + 1;
        end
    end

    // READY watchdog
    integer stall = 0;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (ready === 1'b1) stall = 0;
        else begin
            stall = stall + 1;
            if (stall > 3000000) $fatal(1, "READY stuck low (line %b rect %b circle %b swap %b)", dut.line_busy, dut.rect_busy, dut.circ_busy, dut.swap_pending);
        end
    end

    // swaps must happen exactly at the start of vertical blanking
    reg prev_front = 1'b0;
    integer swaps_seen = 0;
    always @(negedge clk) begin
        if (dut.front_buf !== prev_front && dut.reset !== 1'b1) begin
            if (dut.u_vga.v_count != 480 || dut.u_vga.h_count != 1)
                $fatal(1, "buffer swap outside vblank (v=%0d h=%0d)",
                       dut.u_vga.v_count, dut.u_vga.h_count);
            swaps_seen = swaps_seen + 1;
        end
        prev_front = dut.front_buf;
    end

    // ---------------- software model ----------------
    reg [PIX_BITS-1:0] model [0 : 2*FB_PIXELS-1];
    integer front = 0;           // which model buffer is on screen
    integer model_count;         // pixels the last command should write

    function [PIX_BITS-1:0] conv(input [7:0] c);
        conv = (PIX_BITS == 3) ? {c[7], c[4], c[1]} : c[PIX_BITS-1:0];
    endfunction

    function integer back;
        input dummy;
        back = DOUBLE_BUF ? 1 - front : 0;
    endfunction

    function integer sx12(input [15:0] v);    // 12-bit signed, like the RTL
        sx12 = v[11] ? ($signed({1'b0, v[11:0]}) - 4096) : v[11:0];
    endfunction

    task model_plot(input integer x, input integer y, input [PIX_BITS-1:0] c);
        begin
            if (x >= 0 && x < FB_W && y >= 0 && y < FB_H) begin
                model[back(0) * FB_PIXELS + y * FB_W + x] = c;
                model_count = model_count + 1;
            end
        end
    endtask

    task model_line(input integer x0, y0, x1, y1, input [PIX_BITS-1:0] c);
        integer x, y, dx, dy, sx, sy, err, e2, done;
        begin
            dx = (x1 > x0) ? x1 - x0 : x0 - x1;
            dy = (y1 > y0) ? y0 - y1 : y1 - y0;
            sx = (x0 < x1) ? 1 : -1;
            sy = (y0 < y1) ? 1 : -1;
            err = dx + dy; x = x0; y = y0; done = 0;
            while (!done) begin
                model_plot(x, y, c);
                if (x == x1 && y == y1) done = 1;
                else begin
                    e2 = 2 * err;
                    if (e2 >= dy) begin err = err + dy; x = x + sx; end
                    if (e2 <= dx) begin err = err + dx; y = y + sy; end
                end
            end
        end
    endtask

    task model_rect(input integer x, y, w, h, input [PIX_BITS-1:0] c);
        integer i, j, x0, y0, x1, y1;
        begin
            x0 = (x < 0) ? 0 : x;            y0 = (y < 0) ? 0 : y;
            x1 = (x + w > FB_W) ? FB_W : x + w;
            y1 = (y + h > FB_H) ? FB_H : y + h;
            for (j = y0; j < y1; j = j + 1)
                for (i = x0; i < x1; i = i + 1)
                    model_plot(i, j, c);
        end
    endtask

    // midpoint circle, same step order and span rules as circle_renderer.v
    task model_span(input integer row, xa, xb, input [PIX_BITS-1:0] c);
        integer i;
        begin
            if (xa < 0) xa = 0;
            if (xb > FB_W - 1) xb = FB_W - 1;
            if (row >= 0 && row < FB_H)
                for (i = xa; i <= xb; i = i + 1)
                    model_plot(i, row, c);
        end
    endtask

    task model_circle(input integer cx, cy, r, fill, input [PIX_BITS-1:0] c);
        integer x, y, dd, xn, yn, dn, last;
        begin
            x = r; y = 0; dd = 1 - r; last = 0;
            while (!last) begin
                yn = y + 1;
                xn = (dd < 0) ? x : x - 1;
                dn = (dd < 0) ? dd + 2 * yn + 1 : dd + 2 * (yn - xn) + 1;
                last = (xn < yn);
                if (!fill) begin
                    model_plot(cx + x, cy + y, c);  model_plot(cx + y, cy + x, c);
                    model_plot(cx - y, cy + x, c);  model_plot(cx - x, cy + y, c);
                    model_plot(cx - x, cy - y, c);  model_plot(cx - y, cy - x, c);
                    model_plot(cx + y, cy - x, c);  model_plot(cx + x, cy - y, c);
                end
                else begin
                    model_span(cy + y, cx - x, cx + x, c);
                    if (y != 0)
                        model_span(cy - y, cx - x, cx + x, c);
                    if ((dd >= 0 || last) && x != y) begin
                        model_span(cy + x, cx - y, cx + y, c);
                        model_span(cy - x, cx - y, cx + y, c);
                    end
                end
                x = xn; y = yn; dd = dn;
            end
        end
    endtask

    task model_apply(input [79:0] w);
        reg [7:0] op;
        integer a, b, c, d;
        begin
            op = w[79:72];
            a = sx12(w[71:56]); b = sx12(w[55:40]);
            c = sx12(w[39:24]); d = sx12(w[23:8]);
            model_count = 0;
            case (op)
                8'h01: model_rect(0, 0, FB_W, FB_H, conv(w[7:0]));
                8'h02: model_line(a, b, c, d, conv(w[7:0]));
                8'h03: model_rect(a, b, w[39:24] & 12'hFFF, w[23:8] & 12'hFFF, conv(w[7:0]));
                8'h04: if (DOUBLE_BUF) front = 1 - front;
                8'h05: model_circle(a, b, w[34:24], w[8], conv(w[7:0]));
                default: ;
            endcase
        end
    endtask

    // read one pixel out of the DUT memory (flip-flop array or SRAM macros)
    function [PIX_BITS-1:0] peek(input integer a);
`ifdef SRAM_CFG
        reg [31:0] wd;
        begin
            case (a / 1024)
                0: wd = dut.u_fb.g_bank[0].u_sram.mem[(a % 1024) / 4];
                1: wd = dut.u_fb.g_bank[1].u_sram.mem[(a % 1024) / 4];
                2: wd = dut.u_fb.g_bank[2].u_sram.mem[(a % 1024) / 4];
                3: wd = dut.u_fb.g_bank[3].u_sram.mem[(a % 1024) / 4];
                default: wd = dut.u_fb.g_bank[4].u_sram.mem[(a % 1024) / 4];
            endcase
            peek = wd >> (8 * (a % 4));
        end
`else
        peek = dut.u_fb.mem[a];
`endif
    endfunction

    task compare_back;
        integer i, base;
        begin
            base = DOUBLE_BUF ? (dut.front_buf ? 0 : FB_PIXELS) : 0;
            if (DOUBLE_BUF && dut.front_buf !== front[0])
                $fatal(1, "front buffer mismatch");
            for (i = 0; i < FB_PIXELS; i = i + 1)
                if (peek(base + i) !== model[back(0) * FB_PIXELS + i])
                    $fatal(1, "FB mismatch at pixel %0d (x=%0d y=%0d): dut=%h model=%h",
                           i, i % FB_W, i / FB_W, peek(base + i),
                           model[back(0) * FB_PIXELS + i]);
        end
    endtask

    // ---------------- SPI host ----------------
    task wait_ready;
        begin
            wait (ready === 1'b1);
            @(negedge clk);
            @(negedge clk);     // SRAM macros commit writes half a clock later
        end
    endtask

    task spi_frame(input [79:0] w, input integer nbits);
        integer i;
        begin
            cs_n = 1'b0;
            #(SPI_HALF);
            for (i = 0; i < nbits; i = i + 1) begin
                mosi = (i < 80) ? w[79 - i] : 1'b0;
                #(SPI_HALF) sck = 1'b1;
                #(SPI_HALF) sck = 1'b0;
            end
            #(SPI_HALF) cs_n = 1'b1;
            #(SPI_HALF);
        end
    endtask

    integer n_cmds = 0;

    // send one command, then check write count + whole back buffer
    task exec(input [79:0] w);
        integer wr0;
        begin
            wait_ready;
            model_apply(w);
            wr0 = writes;
            spi_frame(w, 80);
            repeat (8) @(negedge clk);
            wait_ready;
            if (writes - wr0 != model_count)
                $fatal(1, "cmd %h wrote %0d pixels, model says %0d", w, writes - wr0, model_count);
            if (w[79:72] != 8'h04)
                compare_back;
            n_cmds = n_cmds + 1;
        end
    endtask

    function [79:0] mk(input [7:0] op, input integer a, b, c, d, input [7:0] col);
        mk = {op, a[15:0], b[15:0], c[15:0], d[15:0], col};
    endfunction

    // ---------------- VGA frame capture from the pins ----------------
    integer hd1 = 0, vd1 = 0, hd2 = 0, vd2 = 0;
    integer cap_state = 0, cap_fd = 0, cap_errors = 0;
    reg [PIX_BITS-1:0] expect_pix;
    reg expect_hs, expect_vs;

    always @(negedge clk) begin
        // pins at this negedge belong to the counter value seen 2 negedges ago
        if (cap_state == 1 && hd2 == 0 && vd2 == 0)
            cap_state = 2;

        if (cap_state == 2) begin
            expect_hs = !(hd2 >= 656 && hd2 < 752);
            expect_vs = !(vd2 >= 490 && vd2 < 492);
            if (hd2 < 640 && vd2 < 480)
                expect_pix = model[front * FB_PIXELS + (vd2 >> SHIFT) * FB_W + (hd2 >> SHIFT)];
            else
                expect_pix = 0;

            if (pix !== expect_pix || hs !== expect_hs || vs !== expect_vs) begin
                cap_errors = cap_errors + 1;
                if (cap_errors < 5)
                    $display("VGA mismatch at (%0d,%0d): pix=%h exp=%h hs=%b vs=%b",
                             hd2, vd2, pix, expect_pix, hs, vs);
            end
            if (hd2 < 640 && vd2 < 480)
                $fwrite(cap_fd, "%h\n", pix);
            if (hd2 == 799 && vd2 == 524)
                cap_state = 3;
        end

        hd2 = hd1; vd2 = vd1;
        hd1 = dut.u_vga.h_count; vd1 = dut.u_vga.v_count;
    end

    task capture_frame(input [8*128-1:0] fname);
        begin
            cap_fd = $fopen(fname, "w");
            cap_errors = 0;
            cap_state = 1;
            wait (cap_state == 3);
            cap_state = 0;
            $fclose(cap_fd);
            if (cap_errors != 0)
                $fatal(1, "captured frame %0s has %0d mismatches", fname, cap_errors);
            $display("  captured + verified frame -> %0s", fname);
        end
    endtask

    // ---------------- test sequence ----------------
    reg [8*128-1:0] demo_file, frame_prefix, fname;
    reg [79:0] w;
    integer fd, i, r, wr0, frame_no, swaps_in_stream;

    initial begin
        if ($test$plusargs("vcd")) begin
            $dumpfile("build/gpu.vcd");
            $dumpvars(0, tb_gpu);
        end
        if (!$value$plusargs("frames=%s", frame_prefix))
            frame_prefix = "build/frame";

        for (i = 0; i < 2 * FB_PIXELS; i = i + 1) model[i] = 0;

        // ---- 1. reset + power-up clear ----
        #1000;
        if (ready !== 1'b0 || pix !== 0) $fatal(1, "reset: READY/RGB not low");
        rst_n = 1'b1;
        wait_ready;
        if (writes != DEPTH) $fatal(1, "power-up clear wrote %0d, expected %0d", writes, DEPTH);
        compare_back;
        $display("[1] reset + power-up clear of %0d words OK", DEPTH);

        if ($value$plusargs("demo=%s", demo_file)) begin
            // ---------------- demo mode ----------------
            fd = $fopen(demo_file, "r");
            if (fd == 0) $fatal(1, "cannot open %0s", demo_file);
            frame_no = 0; swaps_in_stream = 0;
            while (!$feof(fd)) begin
                r = $fscanf(fd, "%h\n", w);
                if (r == 1) begin
                    exec(w);
                    if (w[79:72] == 8'h04) begin
                        swaps_in_stream = swaps_in_stream + 1;
                        if (DOUBLE_BUF || swaps_in_stream > 1) begin
                            $sformat(fname, "%0s_%03d.hex", frame_prefix, frame_no);
                            capture_frame(fname);
                            frame_no = frame_no + 1;
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
            $fclose(fd);
            $display("PASS: demo %0s, %0d commands, %0d frames", demo_file, n_cmds, frame_no);
            $finish;
        end

        // ---- 2. lines: all 8 octants, axis, point, clipped ----
        exec(mk(8'h01, 0, 0, 0, 0, 8'h00));
        exec(mk(8'h02, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_W-3, FB_H/2+3,  8'hE0));
        exec(mk(8'h02, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_W/2+4, FB_H-2,  8'h1C));
        exec(mk(8'h02, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_W/2-4, FB_H-2,  8'h03));
        exec(mk(8'h02, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, 2, FB_H/2+3,       8'hFC));
        exec(mk(8'h02, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, 2, FB_H/2-3,       8'h1F));
        exec(mk(8'h02, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_W/2-4, 1,       8'hE3));
        exec(mk(8'h02, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_W/2+4, 1,       8'hFF));
        exec(mk(8'h02, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_W-3, FB_H/2-3,  8'hF0));
        exec(mk(8'h02, 0, 0, FB_W-1, 0,                   8'hFF));   // horizontal
        exec(mk(8'h02, FB_W-1, FB_H-1, FB_W-1, 0,         8'hE0));   // vertical
        exec(mk(8'h02, 5, 5, 5, 5,                        8'h1C));   // single point
        exec(mk(8'h02, -20, -10, FB_W+15, FB_H+7,         8'h03));   // clipped both ends
        exec(mk(8'h02, -100, 3, -5, 9,                    8'hFF));   // fully off screen
        $display("[2] line renderer: octants, axis, point, clipping OK");

        // ---- 3. rectangles + clipping ----
        exec(mk(8'h03, 3, 2, 7, 5,                        8'hE0));
        exec(mk(8'h03, -4, -3, 9, 8,                      8'h1C));   // clipped top/left
        exec(mk(8'h03, FB_W-4, FB_H-3, 50, 50,            8'h03));   // clipped bottom/right
        exec(mk(8'h03, 10, 10, 0, 5,                      8'hFF));   // zero width -> nothing
        exec(mk(8'h03, FB_W+5, 2, 4, 4,                   8'hFF));   // off screen -> nothing
        $display("[3] rectangle filler + clipping OK");

        // ---- 4. circles: outline + filled, tiny, clipped, huge, off screen ----
        exec(mk(8'h01, 0, 0, 0, 0, 8'h00));
        exec(mk(8'h05, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_H/3, 0,         8'hFF));   // outline
        exec(mk(8'h05, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_H/5, 1,         8'hE0));   // filled
        exec(mk(8'h05, 4, 4, 0, 0,                        8'h1C));   // r = 0
        exec(mk(8'h05, 8, 4, 0, 1,                        8'h1C));
        exec(mk(8'h05, 4, 9, 1, 0,                        8'h03));   // r = 1
        exec(mk(8'h05, 9, 9, 1, 1,                        8'h03));
        exec(mk(8'h05, -3, 2, 8, 0,                       8'hFC));   // clipped left/top
        exec(mk(8'h05, -3, FB_H/2, 8, 1,                  8'hFC));
        exec(mk(8'h05, FB_W-2, FB_H-1, 10, 1,             8'h1F));   // clipped right/bottom
        exec(mk(8'h05, FB_W-2, 1, 9, 0,                   8'hE3));
        exec(mk(8'h05, -100, -100, 5, 1,                  8'hFF));   // off screen
        exec(mk(8'h05, 2047, -2048, 2047, 0,              8'hFF));   // extreme values
        exec(mk(8'h05, 2047, -2048, 2047, 1,              8'hFF));
        exec(mk(8'h05, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_W, 1,           8'h92));   // covers the screen
        exec(mk(8'h05, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_W, 0,           8'hF0));   // all off screen
        $display("[4] circle renderer: outline, filled, r=0/1, clipping, extremes OK");

        // ---- 5. malformed frames must not write anything ----
        wr0 = writes;
        wait_ready; spi_frame(mk(8'h03, 0, 0, 5, 5, 8'hFF), 79);
        wait_ready; spi_frame(mk(8'h03, 0, 0, 5, 5, 8'hFF), 81);
        wait_ready; spi_frame(mk(8'h7F, 0, 0, 5, 5, 8'hFF), 80);
        repeat (50) @(negedge clk);
        wait_ready;
        if (writes != wr0) $fatal(1, "malformed frame wrote pixels");
        compare_back;
        $display("[5] short / long / unknown frames ignored OK");

        // ---- 6. a frame sent while busy is dropped ----
        model_apply(mk(8'h01, 0, 0, 0, 0, 8'h92));
        wr0 = writes;
        wait_ready;
        spi_frame(mk(8'h01, 0, 0, 0, 0, 8'h92), 80);       // CLEAR (busy for FB_PIXELS clocks)
        spi_frame(mk(8'h03, 0, 0, 4, 4, 8'hE0), 80);       // immediately, no READY check
        repeat (8) @(negedge clk);
        wait_ready;
        if (writes - wr0 != FB_PIXELS) $fatal(1, "busy-drop test wrote %0d", writes - wr0);
        compare_back;
        $display("[6] command during busy dropped OK");

        // ---- 7. build a scene, SWAP, capture a full frame from the pins ----
        exec(mk(8'h01, 0, 0, 0, 0, 8'h00));
        exec(mk(8'h03, 2, 2, FB_W/3, FB_H/3,              8'hE0));
        exec(mk(8'h03, FB_W/2, FB_H/2, FB_W/3, FB_H/3,    8'h1C));
        exec(mk(8'h02, 0, FB_H-1, FB_W-1, 0,              8'hFF));
        exec(mk(8'h02, 0, 0, FB_W-1, FB_H-1,              8'h03));
        exec(mk(8'h05, FB_W*3/4, FB_H/4, FB_H/6, 1,      8'hFC));
        exec(mk(8'h05, FB_W/4, FB_H*3/4, FB_H/6, 0,      8'h1F));
        exec(mk(8'h04, 0, 0, 0, 0, 8'h00));                // SWAP
        if (DOUBLE_BUF && swaps_seen != 1) $fatal(1, "swap did not happen");
        $sformat(fname, "%0s_test.hex", frame_prefix);
        capture_frame(fname);
        $display("[7] SWAP at vblank + full 800x525 frame (pixels, HSYNC, VSYNC) OK");

        // ---- 8. reset again in the middle of things ----
        wait_ready;
        spi_frame(mk(8'h01, 0, 0, 0, 0, 8'hFF), 80);
        #2000;
        rst_n = 1'b0; #500;
        if (ready !== 1'b0) $fatal(1, "READY high in reset");
        wr0 = writes;
        rst_n = 1'b1;
        for (i = 0; i < 2 * FB_PIXELS; i = i + 1) model[i] = 0;
        front = 0;
        wait_ready;
        if (writes - wr0 != DEPTH) $fatal(1, "second power-up clear wrote %0d", writes - wr0);
        compare_back;
        $display("[8] reset during a command + second clear OK");

        $display("PASS: all gpu_core tests (%0dx%0d, %0d-bit, %s buffer), %0d commands",
                 FB_W, FB_H, PIX_BITS, DOUBLE_BUF ? "double" : "single", n_cmds);
        $finish;
    end

endmodule
