# =========================================================
# 02_power.tcl : power nets, core ring, straps, macro hookup
# Run from the chip/ folder:
#     openroad -gui tcl/02_power.tcl
# =========================================================

# =========================================
# Load completed floorplan
# =========================================

read_db "results/01_floorplan.odb"

set PDK $::env(SKY130_PDK)
set HD "$PDK/libs.ref/sky130_fd_sc_hd"

read_liberty \
    "$HD/lib/sky130_fd_sc_hd__tt_025C_1v80.lib"

set Block [ord::get_db_block]

# =========================================
# Mark the supply networks
# =========================================

foreach {Name Type} {
    VCCD  POWER
    VSSD  GROUND
    VDDIO POWER
    VSSIO GROUND
    VDDA  POWER
    VSSA  GROUND
} {
    set Net [$Block findNet $Name]

    if {$Net eq "NULL"} {
        error "Missing supply net: $Name"
    }

    $Net setSpecial
    $Net setSigType $Type
}

# =========================================
# Register power-pin matching rules
# =========================================
# VPWR/VGND also covers the gpu_asic macro and the tap cells.

add_global_connection \
    -net VCCD \
    -pin_pattern {^(VPWR|VPB|VCCD)$} \
    -power

add_global_connection \
    -net VSSD \
    -pin_pattern {^(VGND|VNB|VSSD)$} \
    -ground

add_global_connection \
    -net VDDIO \
    -pin_pattern {^VDDIO$} \
    -power

add_global_connection \
    -net VSSIO \
    -pin_pattern {^VSSIO$} \
    -ground

add_global_connection \
    -net VDDA \
    -pin_pattern {^VDDA$} \
    -power

add_global_connection \
    -net VSSA \
    -pin_pattern {^VSSA$} \
    -ground

global_connect -verbose

# =========================================
# Digital-core voltage domain
# =========================================

set_voltage_domain \
    -name CORE \
    -power VCCD \
    -ground VSSD

# =========================================
# Define the core PDN grid
# =========================================

define_pdn_grid \
    -name CORE_GRID \
    -voltage_domains {CORE}

# =========================================
# Core power ring  (met4 vertical / met5 horizontal)
# -connect_to_pads joins the ring to the VCCD/VSSD pad pins
# =========================================

add_pdn_ring \
    -grid CORE_GRID \
    -layers {met4 met5} \
    -widths {4 4} \
    -spacings {2 2} \
    -core_offsets 10 \
    -connect_to_pads

# =========================================
# Standard-cell power rails (met1, on every row)
# =========================================

add_pdn_stripe \
    -grid CORE_GRID \
    -layer met1 \
    -width 0.48 \
    -followpins \
    -extend_to_core_ring

# =========================================
# Upper metal power straps
# =========================================
# met5 horizontal straps run OVER the macro (the macro only uses
# met1-met4), that is how the macro gets its power.

add_pdn_stripe \
    -grid CORE_GRID \
    -layer met4 \
    -width 1.6 \
    -pitch 48 \
    -offset 20 \
    -extend_to_core_ring

add_pdn_stripe \
    -grid CORE_GRID \
    -layer met5 \
    -width 1.6 \
    -pitch 48 \
    -offset 20 \
    -extend_to_core_ring

# =========================================
# PDN vias
# =========================================

add_pdn_connect \
    -grid CORE_GRID \
    -layers {met1 met4}

add_pdn_connect \
    -grid CORE_GRID \
    -layers {met4 met5}

# =========================================
# Hard macro power grid
# =========================================
# The macro's VPWR/VGND pins are vertical met4 straps.
# Every top-level met5 strap that crosses them gets a met4-met5 via.
# -halo keeps the top-level met4 straps / rails 10 um away from it.

define_pdn_grid \
    -macro \
    -name GPU_GRID \
    -instances {u_core} \
    -starts_with POWER \
    -halo {10 10}

add_pdn_connect \
    -grid GPU_GRID \
    -layers {met4 met5}

# =========================================
# Check and generate PDN
# =========================================

pdngen -check_only

pdngen \
    -failed_via_report reports/02_failed_vias.rpt

# =========================================
# Save
# =========================================

write_db results/02_power.odb
write_def results/02_power.def

puts "Core power network generated."
terminalBashchip/ · devshell

openroad -gui tcl/02_power.tcl

Check in the GUI

  1. Console: Core power network generated. reports/02_failed_vias.rpt should be (nearly) empty; nothing inside the macro outline.
  2. Display Control → Nets: only VCCD. Follow pad → ring → met5 straps → over the macro; zoom at the macro edge: met4-met5 vias on its VPWR straps.

# =========================================================
# 04_streamout.tcl : merge everything into chip_top.gds (Magic)
# Run from the chip/ folder:
#   magic -dnull -noconsole \
#         -rcfile $SKY130_PDK/libs.tech/magic/sky130A.magicrc \
#         tcl/04_streamout.tcl | tee reports/04_streamout.log
# =========================================================

set PDK $::env(SKY130_PDK)

set HD "$PDK/libs.ref/sky130_fd_sc_hd"
set IO "$PDK/libs.ref/sky130_fd_io"

set TechLEF "$HD/techlef/sky130_fd_sc_hd__nom.tlef"

# Technology information, including via definitions
lef read $TechLEF

# Import the actual layout geometry
gds readonly true
gds rescale false

gds read "$HD/gds/sky130_fd_sc_hd.gds"

set BaseIOGDS "$IO/gds/sky130_fd_io.gds"
if {[file exists $BaseIOGDS]} {
    gds read $BaseIOGDS
}

gds read "$IO/gds/sky130_ef_io.gds"

# Load any separately installed GPIO GDS files
foreach File [glob -nocomplain "$IO/gds/*gpiov2*.gds"] {
    gds read $File
}

# The hardened GPU
gds read "macros/gpu_asic.gds"

# Annotate actual GDS cells with LEF pin information
lef read "$HD/lef/sky130_fd_sc_hd.lef" -annotate
lef read "$IO/lef/sky130_fd_io.lef" -annotate
lef read "$IO/lef/sky130_ef_io.lef" -annotate
lef read "macros/gpu_asic.lef" -annotate

# Import placed cells and routed wires
def read "results/03_routed.def"

load chip_top
select top cell

# Produce candidate chip layout
gds write "results/chip_top.gds"

puts "GDS write command finished"
quit -noprompt

# =========================================================
# 06_extract.tcl : top-level connectivity extraction (Magic)
# Cells are loaded as LEF ABSTRACTS, so pads / std cells / the macro
# become black boxes and only the TOP-LEVEL wiring is extracted.
# (The macro itself was already LVS-checked inside LibreLane.)
#
#   magic -dnull -noconsole \
#         -rcfile $SKY130_PDK/libs.tech/magic/sky130A.magicrc \
#         tcl/06_extract.tcl | tee reports/06_extract.log
# =========================================================

set PDK $::env(SKY130_PDK)
set HD "$PDK/libs.ref/sky130_fd_sc_hd"
set IO "$PDK/libs.ref/sky130_fd_io"

lef read "$HD/techlef/sky130_fd_sc_hd__nom.tlef"
lef read "$HD/lef/sky130_fd_sc_hd.lef"
lef read "$IO/lef/sky130_fd_io.lef"
lef read "$IO/lef/sky130_ef_io.lef"
lef read "macros/gpu_asic.lef"

def read "results/03_routed.def"

# give the standard cells their real port order (same as LibreLane does)
readspice "$HD/spice/sky130_fd_sc_hd.spice"

load chip_top
select top cell

extract do local
extract all

ext2spice lvs
ext2spice -o results/chip_top_extracted.spice

puts "Extraction finished"
quit -noprompt

# Same recipe LibreLane uses internally (steps/netgen.py)

    $PDK/libs.tech/netgen/sky130A_setup.tcl \
    reports/06_lvs.log \
    -blackbox

puts "LVS finished, see reports/06_lvs.log"

Likely first mismatch: VDDIO_Q / VSSIO_Q

IO_BUSES ties VDDIO_Q to VDDIO and VSSIO_Q to VSSIO. In the abutted padframe these are separate ring buses. If Netgen reports them merged/split, give them their own nets (wire VDDIO_Q, VSSIO_Q;), mark them POWER/GROUND in 02_power.tcl and rerun from the expand step.

Choose the macro and the banking

read

Your PDK ships OpenRAM macros in libs.ref/sky130_sram_macros:

terminalBashWSL
1
2
ls $SKY130_PDK/libs.ref/sky130_sram_macros/lef/
grep -E "SIZE|PIN" $SKY130_PDK/libs.ref/sky130_sram_macros/lef/sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8.lef | head -40

The design uses sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8: 256 × 32 bit with a byte write mask, port 0 read/write, port 1 read-only — one port for drawing, one for VGA. One byte per pixel (RGB332) → 1,024 pixels per macro, so 80 × 60 = 4,800 pixels → 5 macros.

Macro fact (from its LEF / Verilog)Value
Size479.78 × 397.5 µm
Power pinsvccd1 / vssd1 on met3 + met4
Portsclk0 csb0 web0 wmask0[3:0] addr0[7:0] din0 dout0 · clk1 csb1 addr1[7:0] dout1
Timing modelinputs latched on the rising edge, data out after the falling edge → 1-clock latency

// =============================================================
// frame_buffer (SRAM version) - drop-in replacement for rtl/frame_buffer.v
//
// Same ports and same 1-clock read latency, but the storage is a row of
// OpenRAM macros   sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8
//   port 0 (RW) : draw engines write here      (byte write mask)
//   port 1 (R)  : VGA scan-out reads here      (every clock)
//
// One macro = 256 words x 32 bit = 1024 pixels of 8 bit.
//   pixel address a :  bank = a / 1024, word = a[9:2], byte lane = a[1:0]
//
// 80 x 60 x 8 bit = 4800 pixels -> 5 macros
// =============================================================

module frame_buffer #(
    parameter PIX_BITS  = 8,
    parameter DEPTH     = 4800,
    parameter ADDR_BITS = 13
)(
    input wire clk,

    // Write port
    input wire                 write_en,
    input wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] addr_write,
    input wire [PIX_BITS-1:0]  write_data,

    // Read port
    input  wire [ADDR_BITS-1:0] addr_read,
    output reg  [PIX_BITS-1:0]  read_data
);

    localparam BANKS     = (DEPTH + 1023) / 1024;
    localparam BANK_BITS = (ADDR_BITS > 10) ? ADDR_BITS - 10 : 1;

    // which bank / byte the VGA asked for one clock ago
    reg [BANK_BITS-1:0] rd_bank_d;
    reg [1:0]           rd_lane_d;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        rd_bank_d <= addr_read[ADDR_BITS-1:10];
        rd_lane_d <= addr_read[1:0];
    end

    wire [7:0]  wr_byte = write_data;          // PIX_BITS = 8 in this build
    wire [3:0]  wr_mask = 4'b0001 << addr_write[1:0];
    wire [31:0] rd_word [0:BANKS-1];

    genvar i;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < BANKS; i = i + 1) begin : g_bank

            wire sel_w = write_en && (addr_write[ADDR_BITS-1:10] == i);

            // vccd1 / vssd1 are hooked up by LibreLane (PDN_MACRO_CONNECTIONS),
            // dout0 (read data of the write port) is not needed.
            /* verilator lint_off PINMISSING */
            /* verilator lint_off PINCONNECTEMPTY */
            sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 u_sram (
                // port 0 : write
                .clk0  (clk),
                .csb0  (~sel_w),                 // active low chip select
                .web0  (1'b0),                   // 0 = write
                .wmask0(wr_mask),
                .addr0 (addr_write[9:2]),
                .din0  ({4{wr_byte}}),
                .dout0 (),

                // port 1 : read (always enabled)
                .clk1  (clk),
                .csb1  (1'b0),
                .addr1 (addr_read[9:2]),
                .dout1 (rd_word[i])
            );
            /* verilator lint_on PINCONNECTEMPTY */
            /* verilator lint_on PINMISSING */
        end
    endgenerate

    // pick the byte (combinational after the macro's own output register)
    wire [31:0] sel_word = rd_word[rd_bank_d];

    always @(*) begin
        case (rd_lane_d)
            2'd0: read_data = sel_word[ 7: 0];
            2'd1: read_data = sel_word[15: 8];
            2'd2: read_data = sel_word[23:16];
            default: read_data = sel_word[31:24];
        endcase
    end

endmodule

// =============================================================
// gpu_asic (SRAM version) : 80 x 60, 8-bit RGB332, 5 OpenRAM macros
// 5 inputs + 11 outputs = 16 signal GPIOs
// =============================================================

module gpu_asic (
`ifdef USE_POWER_PINS
    inout  wire VPWR,
    inout  wire VGND,
`endif
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst_n,

    input  wire spi_cs_n,
    input  wire spi_sck,
    input  wire spi_mosi,
    output wire gpu_ready,

    output wire vga_hs,
    output wire vga_vs,
    output wire [7:0] vga_rgb    // RRRGGGBB
);

    gpu_core #(
        .FB_W(80),
        .FB_H(60),
        .SCALE_SHIFT(3),         // 8 x 8 screen pixels per FB pixel
        .PIX_BITS(8),
        .DOUBLE_BUF(0)
    ) u_gpu (
        .clk(clk),
        .rst_n(rst_n),
        .spi_cs_n(spi_cs_n),
        .spi_sck(spi_sck),
        .spi_mosi(spi_mosi),
        .gpu_ready(gpu_ready),
        .vga_hs(vga_hs),
        .vga_vs(vga_vs),
        .vga_pix(vga_rgb),
        /* verilator lint_off PINCONNECTEMPTY */
        .dbg_cmd_toggle()                  // debug LED output, not needed on the chip
        /* verilator lint_on PINCONNECTEMPTY */
    );

endmodule

Verified with the real OpenRAM model

All 8 groups pass (circles included) and so do the 36-frame cube and the 40-frame orbit. The model prints about 136 WARNING: Writing and reading … simultaneously! lines: the VGA happened to read a word in the same clock it was written. On silicon that pixel can be wrong for one frame (16 ms) and is then redrawn — invisible. sim/sram_model_sim.v is a quiet stand-in if you do not have the PDK at hand.

Harden the SRAM version with LibreLane

WSLdevshell

The macros go into MACROS (format checked against the LibreLane 3.0.17 source). Two values must come from your synthesized netlist because Yosys decides the flattened instance names:

  1. Synthesis only: cd asic_sram && librelane config.json --run-tag syn --to Yosys.Synthesis
  2. Find the names: grep -o "[^ ]*u_sram[^ ]*" runs/syn/*-yosys-synthesis/gpu_asic.nl.v | sort -u
  3. Put the five names into instances and one regex matching all five into PDN_MACRO_CONNECTIONS (format regex VDD_NET GND_NET macro_vdd_pin macro_gnd_pin), then run the full flow with a new tag.

!
This block is built differently from v1

The SRAM power pins sit on met3/met4, so the block needs met5 straps over them: PDN_MULTILAYER is true here, with a core ring like your counter8 config_ring.json. At chip level this block then behaves like your counter8 macro (met4 + met5 power pins) — connect it with a macro grid as in counter8 and check in the GUI that ring and straps really meet. Expect a few iterations. Five macros + logic need a ≈1.7 × 1.15 mm block → ≈2.6 × 2.0 mm chip, and 16 GPIO pads (5 in, 3 status/sync, 8 colour).

Glossary

read
TermMeaning here
CDCclock domain crossing — a signal moving between unrelated clocks (here: SPI and reset pins → 25 MHz)
STA / SDCstatic timing analysis / the constraints file it reads (gpu.sdc)
LEF / DEF / GDSabstract cell view (size, pins, blockages) / placed + routed design / final mask geometry
PDNpower distribution network: rings, straps, rails, vias
CTSclock tree synthesis
DRC / LVSdesign-rule check / layout-versus-schematic connectivity check
POR / power-goodsignal that says the supplies are stable; enables the pad drivers
Hard macroa pre-placed-and-routed block (gpu_asic) used as one cell by the chip
RGB332 / RGB1118-bit colour 3-3-2 / 3-bit colour 1-1-1
vblankthe 45 non-visible lines between frames
Bresenhamline algorithm with an integer error term: adds and compares only, one pixel per step
Midpoint circlecircle algorithm: walks one octant, decides each step by the sign of f at the midpoint between two candidate pixels
Octantone eighth of the circle (45°); the other seven are mirror images
Spana horizontal run of pixels on one row (how filled circles are drawn)
AR0 … AR13the PYNQ-Z2 names of its Arduino-connector sockets (an Uno prints 0 … 13)
Loopbackfeeding a circuit's own output back into its input to test the path without the real partner
Clippingdropping (or not walking) the part of a shape that is outside the screen

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
check_circle.py - checks the circle algorithm of rtl/circle_renderer.v
(independent of the RTL and of the testbench model).

    python3 scripts/check_circle.py [max_r]        (default 400)

For every radius 0..max_r:
  1. every outline pixel is within half a pixel of the true circle
     ( |x^2 + y^2 - r^2| <= r )
  2. the outline has no gaps (every pixel has an 8-neighbour, r >= 1)
  3. the filled disc writes no pixel twice
  4. the filled disc is exactly "each row filled between the leftmost and
     the rightmost outline pixel" (so outline and fill always match)
Then prints the clock counts used in the guide.
"""
import math, sys

def steps(r):
    """octant 0 of the midpoint circle: yields (x, y, d, last) per step"""
    x, y, d = r, 0, 1 - r
    while True:
        yn = y + 1
        xn = x if d < 0 else x - 1
        dn = d + 2 * yn + 1 if d < 0 else d + 2 * (yn - xn) + 1
        last = xn < yn
        yield x, y, d, last
        if last:
            return
        x, y, d = xn, yn, dn

def outline(r):
    pts = []
    for x, y, d, last in steps(r):
        pts += [(x, y), (y, x), (-y, x), (-x, y), (-x, -y), (-y, -x), (y, -x), (x, -y)]
    return pts

def spans(r):
    """the spans circle_renderer.v walks in filled mode: (row, half_width)"""
    out = []
    for x, y, d, last in steps(r):
        out.append((y, x))                          # s = 0
        if y != 0:
            out.append((-y, x))                     # s = 1
        if (d >= 0 or last) and x != y:
            out += [(x, y), (-x, y)]                # s = 2, 3
    return out

max_r = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 400
bad = 0
for r in range(max_r + 1):
    out = set(outline(r))
    fill = [(i, row) for row, h in spans(r) for i in range(-h, h + 1)]
    if any(abs(px * px + py * py - r * r) > r for px, py in out):
        bad += 1; print('r =', r, ': outline pixel too far from the circle')
    if r >= 1 and any(not any((px + a, py + b) in out for a in (-1, 0, 1) for b in (-1, 0, 1) if a or b)
                      for px, py in out):
        bad += 1; print('r =', r, ': gap in the outline')
    if len(fill) != len(set(fill)):
        bad += 1; print('r =', r, ': filled disc writes a pixel twice')
    hull = set()
    for row in {py for _, py in out}:
        xs = [px for px, py in out if py == row]
        hull |= {(i, row) for i in range(min(xs), max(xs) + 1)}
    if set(fill) != hull:
        bad += 1; print('r =', r, ': filled disc does not match the outline')

print(f'radii 0..{max_r}:', 'ALL CHECKS PASSED' if not bad else f'{bad} PROBLEM(S)')
print()
print('   r  steps  outline clocks  filled pixels  (pi r^2)  filled clocks   @25 MHz')
for r in (3, 10, 50, 100, 200):
    n = sum(1 for _ in steps(r))
    fp = sum(2 * h + 1 for _, h in spans(r))
    print(f'{r:4d} {n:6d} {8*n:15d} {fp:14d} {math.pi*r*r:9.0f} {fp+4*n:14d} {(fp+4*n)/25e3:8.2f} ms')
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
check_vga_test.py - checks the bring-up step 1 test pictures (bringup/step1_vga/vga_pattern.v)
pixel by pixel against an independent model, and writes PNGs.

    python3 scripts/check_vga_test.py [build/vga_test]

The .hex files come from sim/tb_vga_test.v (run_sims.sh stage 7).
"""
import os, sys

D = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'build/vga_test'
BARS = [0xFFF, 0xFF0, 0x0FF, 0x0F0, 0xF0F, 0xF00, 0x00F, 0x000]

def model(sel, x, y, invert=False):
    cx, cy, ix, iy = x // 40, y // 40, x % 40, y % 40
    if sel == 0:
        c = 0xF00 if x in (0, 639) or y in (0, 479) else (0x000 if (cx ^ cy) & 1 else 0xFFF)
    elif sel == 1:
        c = BARS[cx // 2] if y < 320 else cx * 0x111
    elif sel == 2:
        c = [cx << 8, cx << 4, cx, cx * 0x111][min(y // 120, 3)]
    else:
        c = 0xFFF if ix == 0 or iy == 0 or x == 639 or y == 479 or x == 320 or y == 240 else 0x000
    return c ^ 0xFFF if invert else c

cases = [(0, 0, False, 'checkerboard'), (1, 1, False, 'colour bars + grey ramp'), (2, 2, False, 'DAC ramps'),
         (3, 3, False, 'grid'), (4, 0, True, 'inverted checkerboard')]
bad = 0
for n, sel, inv, name in cases:
    px = [int(l, 16) for l in open(f'{D}/pattern_{n}.hex').read().split()]
    if len(px) != 640 * 480:
        print(f'pattern {n}: {len(px)} pixels'); bad += 1; continue
    wrong = sum(1 for i, p in enumerate(px) if p != model(sel, i % 640, i // 640, inv))
    print(f'pattern {n} ({name:24s}): {"OK" if not wrong else str(wrong) + " pixels differ"}')
    bad += wrong != 0
    try:
        from PIL import Image
        im = Image.new('RGB', (640, 480))
        im.putdata([(((p >> 8) & 15) * 17, ((p >> 4) & 15) * 17, (p & 15) * 17) for p in px])
        im.save(f'{D}/pattern_{n}.png')
    except ImportError:
        pass
print('RESULT:', 'ALL 5 PICTURES MATCH THE MODEL' if not bad else f'{bad} PROBLEM(S)')
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

// tb_vga_test : bring-up step 1 bitstream (vga_test_top) in simulation
//
// Captures one full 640x480 frame from the VGA pins for every
// picture: checkerboard (after reset), colour bars (BTN2),
// DAC ramps (BTN3), grid (SW1), inverted checkerboard (BTN1 + SW0).
// Each pixel is written as 3 hex digits RGB444 to
// build/vga_test/pattern_<n>.hex; scripts/check_vga_test.py compares
// every pixel with an independent model and makes the PNGs.
// =============================================================
module tb_vga_test;
    reg sysclk = 1'b0, btn0 = 1'b1;
    reg [2:0] btn = 3'b000;
    reg [1:0] sw  = 2'b00;
    wire hs, vs; wire [3:0] r, g, b, led;

    vga_test_top dut (.sysclk(sysclk), .reset(btn0), .btn(btn), .sw(sw),
                      .vga_hs(hs), .vga_vs(vs), .vga_r(r), .vga_g(g), .vga_b(b), .led(led));

    always #20 sysclk = !sysclk;                   // 25 MHz through the clk_wiz stand-in

    // capture: pins carry the pixel of the counters seen 2 clocks earlier
    integer hd1 = 0, vd1 = 0, hd2 = 0, vd2 = 0, st = 0, fd = 0, hs_low = 0, n_hs = 0;
    always @(negedge sysclk) begin
        if (st == 1 && hd2 == 0 && vd2 == 0) st = 2;
        if (st == 2) begin
            if (hd2 < 640 && vd2 < 480) $fwrite(fd, "%h%h%h\n", r, g, b);
            if (vd2 == 100 && hd2 >= 640 && hs === 1'b0) hs_low = hs_low + 1;  // HSYNC width
            if (hd2 == 799 && vd2 == 524) st = 3;
        end
        hd2 = hd1; vd2 = vd1;
        hd1 = dut.u_vga.h_count; vd1 = dut.u_vga.v_count;
    end

    task capture(input [8*48-1:0] fname);
        begin
            fd = $fopen(fname, "w"); st = 1;
            wait (st == 3); st = 0; $fclose(fd);
        end
    endtask

    task press(input integer k);
        begin
            @(negedge sysclk) btn[k] = 1'b1;
            repeat (10) @(negedge sysclk);
            btn[k] = 1'b0;
        end
    endtask

    initial begin
        repeat (50) @(negedge sysclk);
        btn0 = 1'b0;
        wait (dut.top_reset === 1'b0);                 // clock locked, reset released
        repeat (5) @(negedge sysclk);
        capture("build/vga_test/pattern_0.hex");      // checkerboard right after reset
        if (hs_low != 96) $fatal(1, "HSYNC low for %0d clocks, expected 96", hs_low);
        $display("[1] checkerboard after reset, HSYNC pulse = %0d clocks", hs_low);
        press(1); capture("build/vga_test/pattern_1.hex");
        $display("[2] BTN2: colour bars + grey ramp");
        press(2); capture("build/vga_test/pattern_2.hex");
        $display("[3] BTN3: DAC ramps");
        sw[1] = 1'b1; repeat (10) @(negedge sysclk);
        capture("build/vga_test/pattern_3.hex");
        $display("[4] SW1: 1-pixel grid");
        sw[1] = 1'b0; sw[0] = 1'b1; press(0);
        capture("build/vga_test/pattern_4.hex");
        $display("[5] BTN1 + SW0: inverted checkerboard");
        $display("PASS: step 1 (VGA controller + adapter) frames captured");
        $finish;
    end
endmodule

`timescale 1ns / 1ps
// =============================================================
// tb_selftest : the PYNQ-Z2 top level with its on-board SPI test host
//
// Runs fpga_top (real file, Clocking Wizard replaced by sim/clk_wiz_sim.v)
// as it is built in bring-up step 2, 3 or 4 (iverilog -DSTEP=n, compiled
// with that step's gpu_core.v and engine files, -DROM="<its selftest.mem>"):
//   the power-up test (test 1 runs by itself with SW0 = 1),
//   tests 1..6 by "pressing" BTN1..BTN3 with SW1 down and up
//   (step 2: tests 4..6 are empty - checked that they send nothing),
//   then test 2 again with SW0 = 0 and the SPI header wired back into the
//   Arduino header pins (the loopback test).
// After each test one VGA frame is captured to build/selftest/board_<n>.hex.
// run_sims.sh compares them with frames that tb_gpu.v verified against its
// golden model for the same commands.
// =============================================================
`ifndef STEP
`define STEP 4
`endif
`ifndef ROM
`define ROM "fpga/selftest.mem"
`endif
module tb_selftest;
    reg        sysclk = 1'b0;
    reg        btn0   = 1'b1;          // reset held
    reg  [2:0] btn    = 3'b000;
    reg  [1:0] sw     = 2'b01;         // SW0 = 1: internal test host
    reg        loopback = 1'b0;        // jumper wires SPI header -> AR10/11/13

    wire t_cs, t_sck, t_mosi, ready, hs, vs;
    wire [3:0] r, g, b, led;

    // what the Arduino header sees: the loopback wires, or nothing (pulls)
    wire ar10 = loopback ? t_cs   : 1'b1;
    wire ar13 = loopback ? t_sck  : 1'b0;
    wire ar11 = loopback ? t_mosi : 1'b0;

    fpga_top #(.DEBOUNCE_BITS(4), .ROM_FILE(`ROM)) dut (
        .sysclk(sysclk), .reset(btn0), .btn(btn), .sw(sw),
        .spi_cs_n(ar10), .spi_sck(ar13), .spi_mosi(ar11), .gpu_ready(ready),
        .test_cs_n(t_cs), .test_sck(t_sck), .test_mosi(t_mosi),
        .vga_hs(hs), .vga_vs(vs), .vga_r(r), .vga_g(g), .vga_b(b), .led(led)
    );

    always #20 sysclk = !sysclk;       // 25 MHz (the stand-in passes it through)

    // ---------------- frame capture (same alignment as tb_gpu.v) ----------------
    integer hd1 = 0, vd1 = 0, hd2 = 0, vd2 = 0, cap_state = 0, cap_fd = 0;
    always @(negedge sysclk) begin
        if (cap_state == 1 && hd2 == 0 && vd2 == 0) cap_state = 2;
        if (cap_state == 2) begin
            if (hd2 < 640 && vd2 < 480) $fwrite(cap_fd, "%h\n", dut.pix);
            if (hd2 == 799 && vd2 == 524) cap_state = 3;
        end
        hd2 = hd1; vd2 = vd1;
        hd1 = dut.u_gpu.u_vga.h_count; vd1 = dut.u_gpu.u_vga.v_count;
    end

    task capture(input [8*64-1:0] fname);
        begin
            cap_fd = $fopen(fname, "w");
            cap_state = 1;
            wait (cap_state == 3);
            cap_state = 0;
            $fclose(cap_fd);
        end
    endtask

    // press a button long enough for the debouncer, then wait for the test
    task run_test(input integer n);
        integer k;
        begin
            k = (n - 1) % 3;
            sw[1] = (n > 3);
            @(negedge sysclk) btn[k] = 1'b1;
            wait (dut.test_busy === 1'b1);
            repeat (100) @(negedge sysclk);
            btn[k] = 1'b0;
            wait (dut.test_busy === 1'b0);
            wait (ready === 1'b1);              // last command (the SWAP) done
        end
    endtask

    reg [8*64-1:0] fname;
    integer n, cmds0;
    initial begin
        repeat (50) @(negedge sysclk);
        btn0 = 1'b0;                            // release BTN0
        wait (ready === 1'b1);
        $display("[1] step %0d: reset released, power-up clear done, READY = 1", `STEP);

        // power-up picture: test 1 starts by itself because SW0 = 1
        wait (dut.test_busy === 1'b1);
        wait (dut.test_busy === 1'b0);
        wait (ready === 1'b1);
        capture("build/selftest/auto.hex");
        $display("[2] power-up: test 1 ran by itself, %0d commands", n_cmds);

        for (n = 1; n <= 6; n = n + 1) begin
            cmds0 = n_cmds;
            if (`STEP == 2 && n > 3) begin
                // step 2 has no earlier step: tests 4..6 are empty
                run_test(n);
                repeat (2000) @(negedge sysclk);
                if (n_cmds != cmds0) $fatal(1, "empty test %0d sent %0d commands", n, n_cmds - cmds0);
                $display("[3] test %0d: empty, sends nothing (as it should in step 2)", n);
            end
            else begin
                run_test(n);
                $sformat(fname, "build/selftest/board_%0d.hex", n);
                capture(fname);
                $display("[3] test %0d: %0d commands over SPI, frame -> %0s", n, n_cmds - cmds0, fname);
            end
        end

        // loopback: GPU listens to the Arduino header, test host drives the SPI header
        sw[0] = 1'b0; loopback = 1'b1;
        cmds0 = n_cmds;
        run_test(2);
        capture("build/selftest/board_2_loop.hex");
        $display("[4] loopback (SPI header -> AR10/AR11/AR13, SW0 = 0): test 2, %0d commands", n_cmds - cmds0);
        $display("PASS: bring-up step %0d: power-up test + 6 tests + loopback", `STEP);
        $finish;
    end

    // count completed SPI frames seen by the GPU
    integer n_cmds = 0;
    always @(posedge sysclk) if (dut.u_gpu.cmd_valid) n_cmds = n_cmds + 1;

    initial begin
        #2_000_000_000;                         // 2 s simulated: something is stuck
        $fatal(1, "timeout (test_busy %b, ready %b)", dut.test_busy, ready);
    end
endmodule

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn a captured VGA frame (.hex, 640x480 lines) into a PNG.
   python3 scripts/hex2png.py <fpga|asic|sram> build/fpga_test.hex out.png
   needs:  pip install pillow --break-system-packages
"""
import sys
from PIL import Image
kind, src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
vals = [int(l, 16) for l in open(src) if l.strip()]
img = Image.new('RGB', (640, 480))
px = []
for v in vals:
    if kind in ('fpga', 'sram'):                   # RGB332 -> RGB444 -> 8 bit
        r4 = ((v >> 5) << 1) | (v >> 7)
        g4 = (((v >> 2) & 7) << 1) | ((v >> 4) & 1)
        b4 = ((v & 3) << 2) | (v & 3)
        px.append((r4 * 17, g4 * 17, b4 * 17))
    else:                                          # RGB111
        px.append((255 * ((v >> 2) & 1), 255 * ((v >> 1) & 1), 255 * (v & 1)))
img.putdata(px)
img.save(dst)
print('wrote', dst)

`timescale 1ns / 1ps
// SIMULATION-ONLY behavioural stand-in for the OpenRAM macro, written to
// match the PDK model's timing: inputs captured on posedge, data out on the
// following negedge (so it is valid at the next posedge = 1 clk latency).
// For real work use $SKY130_PDK/libs.ref/sky130_sram_macros/verilog/*.v
module sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 (
    input clk0, input csb0, input web0, input [3:0] wmask0, input [7:0] addr0,
    input [31:0] din0, output reg [31:0] dout0,
    input clk1, input csb1, input [7:0] addr1, output reg [31:0] dout1
);
    reg [31:0] mem [0:255];
    reg csb0_r, web0_r, csb1_r; reg [3:0] wm_r; reg [7:0] a0_r, a1_r; reg [31:0] d0_r;
    always @(posedge clk0) begin csb0_r <= csb0; web0_r <= web0; wm_r <= wmask0; a0_r <= addr0; d0_r <= din0; end
    always @(posedge clk1) begin csb1_r <= csb1; a1_r <= addr1; end
    always @(negedge clk0) if (!csb0_r && !web0_r) begin
        if (wm_r[0]) mem[a0_r][ 7: 0] <= d0_r[ 7: 0];
        if (wm_r[1]) mem[a0_r][15: 8] <= d0_r[15: 8];
        if (wm_r[2]) mem[a0_r][23:16] <= d0_r[23:16];
        if (wm_r[3]) mem[a0_r][31:24] <= d0_r[31:24];
    end
    always @(negedge clk1) if (!csb1_r) dout1 <= mem[a1_r];
endmodule
